ABOUT THE TEAM

At Anduril, we are developing unmanned systems for subsurface, surface, land, and air domains that will leverage unsupervised autonomy for the delivery of multi-mission capability to our customers. Deciding what to build — and in what order — requires people who can connect operational problems, threat-informed scenarios, customer needs, and product employment concepts to the capability we field. We are looking for a Mission Operations Engineer to do that work at the enterprise level, based at our Costa Mesa, California headquarters.

ABOUT THE JOB

Our next Mission Operations Engineer has built and executed plans in the maritime domain, has stood watch, and has been to sea, preferably using uncrewed systems. That background is what separates an analytic product that operators recognize as real from one that reads well and gets ignored. Equally important is the ability to carry that work into a room of senior military and civilian decision-makers and hold it there: this role briefs Commanding Officers, high-level civilians, and our own executive team, and it is expected to give direct answers under hard questioning.

Customer engagement is key, with opportunity to embed directly with our warfighters to provide real-time analysis and feedback on Anduril products. You will normalize how mission problems are framed so that competing programs can be compared on the same terms, and so that investment, roadmap, and capture decisions rest on a defensible operational argument rather than on whichever program briefed most recently.

Being co-located with product leadership, engineering leads, growth, and program directors is the point of the job. You will spend your days in the rooms where trades get made: pressure-testing a concept of employment with the engineers who have to build it, reconciling a program director’s field reality with a product lead’s roadmap, and giving executives the one-page operational case they need to commit capital. Expect up to 50% travel across company facilities, test and demonstration sites, waterfront and fleet concentration areas, and customer locations — the analysis has to survive contact with the water, not just the whiteboard.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Represent the operational perspective in cross-functional reviews, gate decisions, and portfolio planning cycles, and serve as a trusted interpreter between customer language, operational need, product strategy, and engineering implications
  • Partner with systems analysts, engineers, operators, program directors, and business-line leaders to ensure technical solutions remain anchored to real warfighting needs as programs mature
  • Convert results from at-sea demonstrations, field test events, and program execution into portfolio-level lessons that change what we build, closing the loop between the deck plate and the roadmap
  • Understand the enterprise-level mission analysis for the maritime portfolio — identify operational problems, capability gaps, and opportunities for differentiated system employment, and maintain a coherent picture of them across programs rather than one program at a time and be able to communicate them to the customer across the Maritime suite of products
  • Develop and refine concepts of operation, concepts of employment, operational vignettes, mission threads, and use cases for current and future systems, and keep them current as designs and customer priorities move
  • Inform capability roadmaps, IRAD and investment prioritization, and product-market fit assessments by making the operational case for where the next dollar and the next engineer should go
  • Analyze threat environments, customer missions, force structure, operational constraints, and campaign-level context, and translate that context into capability priorities and defensible requirements for product and engineering teams
  • Compare alternative capability approaches and assess trade-offs in mission utility, feasibility, scalability, cost, survivability, and operational relevance — including the approaches we should decline to pursue

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of experience supporting maritime, undersea, or autonomous systems mission areas; experience across air, surface, C2, ISR, fires, or logistics is also valued
  • 5+ years of maritime operational planning experience — building, staffing, and executing operational or campaign plans in the maritime domain at a unit, strike group, numbered fleet, MOC, or component command level
  • Experience tactically employing AUV capabilities or equivalent autonomous system experience including water space coordination in the undersea domain
  • Demonstrated ability to brief and defend operational objectives, and platform capabilities and limitations in front of senior military and civilian decision-makers —Commanding Officers, high-level civilians, and corporate executives — including under direct and skeptical questioning
  • Ability to decompose ambiguous operational problems into structured executable strategies at the tactical level
  • Strong understanding of maritime missions, operational concepts, threat-informed planning, and the relationship between technology and warfighting outcomes
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce executive-level briefings
  • Demonstrated ability to influence decisions across technical, operational, and business stakeholders without owning them — this role earns its authority through the quality of its analysis
  • Ability to hold a portfolio-level view: comfort working several programs, mission areas, and time horizons in parallel and prioritizing among them
  • Strong judgment, intellectual curiosity, and comfort operating with incomplete information in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to translate between customer language, operational need, product strategy, and engineering implications
  • Willingness to travel up to 50% to multiple company facilities, test and demonstration sites, customer locations, and at-sea or field events
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Watch floor experience — TAO, watch officer, battle watch captain, or equivalent time in a maritime operations center, fleet or component watch floor, or afloat combat information center, where decisions were made on incomplete information against a clock
  • Significant at-sea operational experience, including underway deployments, and credibility with the operators who will employ these systems
  • Prior military, DoD, defense industry, intelligence community, operational test, or tactical level development experience
  • Familiarity with CONOPS development, campaign analysis, wargaming, modeling and simulation, operational test, or requirements development
  • Experience working directly with government customers, senior military leaders, product teams, or engineering organizations
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance.

We are scaling at an historic pace, anchored by Arsenal-2, our new software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base.

Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. At the same time, it will build the industrial muscle to field our next-generation AUVs at scale.

We aren't waiting for the new shipyard to be completed. The work on this transformation starts right now, with development inside our new 160,000 square foot Proto-Factory in Orange County, California, where the team is already laying the foundation. As the prototyping hub for Arsenal-2, this facility gives us a multi-year head start, proving out the advanced manufacturing methods, digital workflows, and quality systems that will scale across our broader shipyard network.

In Anduril's Maritime Division, we are actively building America's next decisive advantage at sea—and this is the moment to join us.

ABOUT THE JOB

You will own mechanical design for payloads carried by a maritime autonomous vehicle. Reporting to the Payload Lead, you will design payload housings, mounting structures, and the mechanical interfaces that let Anduril and third-party payloads integrate into the vehicle — pressure-rated, volume-constrained, and swappable in the field. Payload bays are among the most contested real estate on the vehicle, and this role owns making them work.

Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own mechanical design of payload housings, enclosures, and mounting structures.
  • Design pressure-rated payload containment and penetrations for full-depth operation.
  • Define modular mechanical interfaces that enable rapid payload swap in the field.
  • Manage volume, mass, and center-of-gravity budgets for payload installations.
  • Perform structural and pressure analysis on payload assemblies.
  • Produce drawings, tolerance stackups, and interface control documents for payload hardware.
  • Partner with Payload Electrical, Vehicle Interoperability, and Buoyancy & Trim on integration constraints.
  • Support prototype builds, integration testing, and at-sea validation.
  • Travel up to 25% to test sites and supplier facilities.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent.
  • 5+ years of mechanical design experience on hardware that was built and deployed.
  • Strong CAD proficiency and drawing release experience with GD&T.
  • Experience designing sealed, pressure-rated, or environmentally protected enclosures.
  • Working knowledge of structural analysis and hand calculations for load paths.
  • Experience managing mass, volume, and CG budgets under tight constraints.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.
  • Experience with subsea, marine, or deep-submergence mechanical design.
  • Familiarity with underwater connectors, penetrators, and pressure housings.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with subsea, marine, or deep-submergence mechanical design.
  • Familiarity with underwater connectors, penetrators, and pressure housings.
  • Experience with modular or field-swappable hardware interfaces.
  • Background in payload integration for aircraft, spacecraft, or unmanned vehicles.
  • Experience in defense programs or third-party hardware integration.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Air Defense team builds robots that find other robots and knock them out of the sky. At a time when air superiority can no longer be taken for granted, the Air Defense team provides mission-critical capabilities to warfighters. From detection to tracking, identification, deterrence, and defeat, our family of networked sensors and effectors enables our customers to rapidly close the kill chain against a broad range of uncrewed aerial system (UAS) threats.

The Counter-Intrusion business line works on products that enable operators to protect their people and assets from threats on land and sea. We are deployed in every major global operating theater and support a diversity of mission sets across both U.S. Government and allied partners.

Sentry is the primary product focus of this role and it is fielded across both business lines. The Sentry platform integrates robotics, autonomy, hardware, and software to deliver mission-critical capabilities in defense and security, with a rapidly growing fleet and new variants in development. Product Operations is the team that keeps that fleet healthy once it leaves the factory, working across product, engineering, deployment operations, logistics, and sustainment to turn what happens in the field into actionable improvements.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Product Operations Engineer supporting Air Defense and Counter Intrusion, you will be the architect behind how we observe, maintain, and evolve the deployed Sentry fleet. Where others respond to incidents, you build the systems, queries, and processes that enable prevention. You will develop a deep product understanding, serving as a function SME for all things Sentry. You will work with product engineering partners to design, deploy, and improve a system that supports RCCA cycle execution and delivers actionable product improvement signal, directly impacting the design of next generation hardware and software. You will develop and deploy uptime reporting and observability tooling to measure and facilitate capability availability for customers. You will manage and democratize the Sentry knowledge base for field operations functions and support the proliferation of self service resources.

You should bring strong technical depth in robotics engineering, experience leading iterative design across multiple teams, a systems approach to problem solving, and a familiarity with reliability and quality methodologies such as FRACAS. If you are passionate about ground-breaking technology, contributing to the national security mission, and engineering operational excellence from the ground up, Anduril is interested in speaking with you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Product Subject Matter Expertise: Build and hold deep technical understanding of the Sentry system, hardware and software, and serve as the product operations SME for Sentry across both business lines, helping technical and non-technical stakeholders understand each other.

RCCA Cycle Design and Execution: Partner with product engineering to design, deploy, and continuously improve the system that drives root cause corrective action (RCCA) cycles on fielded Sentry towers, from failure capture through corrective action deployment.

Product Improvement Signal: Turn fleet failure data, field feedback, and reliability trends into actionable product improvement signal for engineering, directly informing the design of next generation Sentry hardware and software.

Reliability and Quality Methodology: Apply and mature failure reporting, analysis, and corrective action (FRACAS) practice for Sentry, establishing how failures are classified, tracked, and closed so reliability improvement is measurable rather than anecdotal.

Uptime Reporting and Capability Availability: Develop and deploy uptime reporting that measures and facilitates capability availability for customers, translating raw telemetry into fleet health metrics that program, product, and leadership stakeholders act on.

Observability Tooling: Proactively build and improve the observability tooling behind that reporting in partnership with hardware and software engineering, so coverage keeps pace with new Sentry variants and new site deployments.

Sentry Knowledge Base: Own, democratize, and continuously improve the Sentry knowledge base for field operations functions, so operational knowledge is codified, accurate, and usable by any level of on call support.

Self Service Enablement: Expand the self service resources, runbooks, SOPs, and troubleshooting guides that field and deployment teams rely on, so more is resolved at the point of need and the escalations that do arrive are better characterized.

Iterative Design Across Teams: Lead iterative design cycles spanning product operations, engineering, and deployment functions, building agreement on what to change next and carrying it through to implementation.

  • 5+ years of experience in product operations, technical support, site reliability, or a comparable technical operations role supporting deployed hardware and software systems, with demonstrated progression in scope and ownership
  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, or another relevant technical field, or equivalent hands-on technical experience (military, industrial, or field support)
  • Technical depth in robotics, mechatronics, or complex electromechanical systems, including the ability to reason across hardware, software, and networking boundaries
  • Demonstrated experience driving root cause corrective action (RCCA) to closure on complex systems, including how failures are captured, classified, and verified as resolved
  • Experience leading iterative design or improvement cycles across multiple engineering and operations teams, carrying a change from problem statement through implementation
  • Proficiency developing monitoring queries, dashboards, and alerting configurations using observability platforms such as Datadog, Grafana, or similar tooling
  • Experience validating and verifying software changes on distributed or fielded systems, including rollout, verification, and rollback considerations
  • Scripting and automation skills (e.g., Python, Bash) with a track record of building tooling that improves operational efficiency, plus fluency with development and issue tracking tooling such as Git and Jira
  • Demonstrated ability to author clear, thorough technical documentation including runbooks, SOPs, and troubleshooting guides for both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Ability to coordinate technical and non-technical efforts across product, engineering, deployment, and sustainment functions, including across more than one program or customer at a time
  • Proven ability to work independently, identify what needs to be built, and deliver it without close direction
  • Excellent written, visual, and verbal communication skills
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

  • Familiarity with reliability and quality methodologies such as FRACAS, FMEA, or equivalent structured failure analysis practice
  • Experience with Linux system administration and command-line troubleshooting of electromechanical or networked systems

ABOUT THE JOB 

Own the deployment lifecycle for Anduril compute infrastructure. You will lead the planning, deployment, and sustainment of Anduril hardware nodes—including Menace-T, Menace-I, Voyager compute devices, and 3P server configurations—at government sites nationwide. This includes coordinating site surveys, managing installation activities, conducting acceptance testing, and ensuring each deployment meets mission requirements. You will develop and maintain the processes that turn a one-time installation into a repeatable, scalable deployment capability. 

Serve as the technical bridge between government customers and Anduril engineering. You are the primary liaison for our government stakeholders, translating their operational needs into actionable engineering requirements and keeping them informed on delivery timelines, integration status, and system performance. You will represent the customer perspective in internal planning sessions and ensure Anduril’s engineering teams have the context they need to build the right solutions. 

Drive third-party system integration. Work with partner organizations to integrate sensors, effectors, and other third-party systems into Anduril hardware form factors. You will assess power, cooling, weight, and rack-space requirements; coordinate integration testing; and ensure deployed configurations meet both Anduril and government specifications. 

Build and formalize fleet management. Stand up and own a fleet management capability for deployed Anduril nodes. This includes tracking hardware assets from procurement through deployment, maintaining configuration records, monitoring system health in coordination with SRE teams, and building the reporting and dashboards that give program leadership visibility into the state of the fleet. 

Partner with Software Engineering and SRE teams. Collaborate closely with software engineers and site reliability engineers to ensure deployed hardware is running the correct software baselines, that updates are applied efficiently, and that operational issues are triaged and resolved quickly. You will participate in incident response and help shape the processes that keep our systems healthy at scale.

  • Assess and coordinate the physical integration of third-party sensors and effectors into Anduril hardware form factors, including power, cooling, network, and rack-space requirements

  • Partner with SRE teams to monitor deployed node health, coordinate software updates, and support incident response 
  • Create and deliver technical reports, deployment readiness reviews, and status briefings for government and internal leadership 
  • Drive continuous improvement of deployment processes, documentation, and playbooks to enable repeatable, scalable site activations 
  • Support program management activities including schedule tracking, risk identification, and deliverable management 
  • Contribute to the development of training materials and conduct end-user training at deployed sites

  • Technical familiarity with hardware form factors used in defense deployments, including rack-mount servers, ruggedized edge compute devices, and mobile computing platforms 
  • Understanding of how third-party systems (sensors, effectors, C2 systems) integrate into compute hardware, including power, cooling, and networking requirements 
  • Demonstrated ability to serve as a liaison between technical engineering teams and government customers, with strong stakeholder management skills 
  • Experience working alongside software engineers and/or SRE teams on deployment, integration, or operational readiness activities 
  • Strong organizational skills with experience tracking assets, configurations, or fleet-level data across distributed sites 
  • Ability to travel 25–50% to government sites for deployments, site surveys, and customer engagements

ABOUT THE TEAM

Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build the software-defined shipyard. That means the full technology stack running Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, ArsenalOS (our manufacturing execution system that workers and planners use every shift), the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that eliminate manual toil from both the shop floor and business operations.

This work is anchored by Arsenal-2, our software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base. ArsenalOS is the digital backbone of that yard. It connects fabrication and outfitting to material movement and inspection. Planners get one real-time view of production. We aren't waiting for the yard to open. Development is already underway here in Orange County, California. The team is proving out the manufacturing methods and digital workflows that will scale across the shipyard network.

MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology. Our systems live where factory-floor machines, edge compute, and OT networks meet enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure. We incubate solutions close to the production line, validate them with real operators building real hardware, harden them for reliability and security, and then scale them across multiple sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship.

This is not a support function. It is a strategic investment by Anduril in the premise that digitizing the manufacturing lifecycle end-to-end, from engineering definition through scheduling through execution through field feedback, is how Heavy Metal will out-build, out-adapt, and out-scale the traditional defense industrial base. MDP is scaling from a founding team to 70+ engineers across multiple U.S. sites. You will be joining early, working on hard problems with real operational stakes, and shaping how manufacturing software is built at Anduril from the ground up.

ABOUT THE JOB

MDP is building the manufacturing digital thread that connects engineering release to the machines and inspection systems on the factory floor. You'll own the Development and integration integration layer between Teamcenter and Anduril's ArsenalOS platform so CAM programs, CAI/CMM programs, tools and fixtures, and inspection results move automatically instead of by hand.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Build and own the integrations that carry CAM and CAI data out of Teamcenter and onto the shop floor, including NX CAM outputs, DNC dispatch to machine controls and the return path for as-run data.

  • Close the inspection loop by integrating CAI and metrology systems so measured results land back in the digital thread as structured data rather than static reports.
  • Make EBOM to MBOM propagation and model-based definition data flow automatically into downstream manufacturing and quality systems.
  • Unblock partner teams across scheduling, applied AI and manufacturing systems by exposing manufacturing data through APIs they can build on.
  • Partner with manufacturing engineers and factory operators to understand production workflows and translate them into software requirements.
  • Write production-quality code with comprehensive tests, participating in code review and architectural discussions.
  • Deploy and operate your systems in factory environments, including edge compute clusters and OT networks.
  • Leverage AI tooling (coding assistants, automation) in your development workflow and contribute to team engineering practices.
  • Join an on-call rotation supporting production factory systems.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of experience in a software engineering role building production systems, ideally in a fast-paced environment.
  • Deep expertise in Teamcenter development: 5+ years hands-on with ITK and SOA customization in C++ and Java, BMIDE data modeling and Active Workspace.
  • Demonstrated experience building custom Teamcenter handlers, services and integrations, not only configuring workflows and templates.
  • Working knowledge of manufacturing data domains, including CAM, CAI, CMM, and NC programming outputs, machine dispatch, metrology and inspection data, and the relationship between EBOM and MBOM.
  • Experience authoring and developing NX Open programs to automate NX/Design Center workflows.
  • Strong technical fluency in modern software architectures, APIs, distributed systems, CI/CD, and cloud or edge infrastructure.
  • Experience building systems that must operate reliably under real-world operational constraints (high availability, low latency, or constrained environments).
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across engineering, manufacturing, and operations teams.
  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related technical field, or equivalent practical
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in manufacturing, industrial, or OT-adjacent domains (MES, SCADA, PLC integration, factory automation, IoT).
  • Hands-on experience with CAM and CAI toolchains such as NX CAM, Vericut and PolyWorks, and with industrial data protocols such as MTConnect and OPC-UA.
  • Familiarity with model-based definition standards including STEP AP242, ASME Y14.41 and CAD PMI, and with QIF for inspection data exchange.
  • Familiarity with frontier AI tooling, AI coding assistants, and AI-enabled software development workflows.
  • Experience in hyper-growth startup-like environments, with demonstrated success balancing speed, ambiguity, and long-term system health.
  • Familiarity with enterprise systems such as ERP, MES, WMS, or manufacturing planning systems.

ABOUT THE TEAM 

The Software Integration Environment (SIE) team builds the platform Anduril uses to test software the way it will actually be flown, driven, and fought: real binaries, running on real services, under conditions we control. We provision isolated, reproducible environments for simulation and integration testing at scale, across AWS, Azure, and on-premise. The platform is used both internally by Anduril engineers and externally by our customers. Compute was the first half of that problem. The second half is the simulated world those binaries run inside — how it gets authored, how heterogeneous simulators agree on it, and how an engineer inspects and trusts what happened during a run. That is what this role owns.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer with deep C++ and real-time systems experience to build the simulation layer of the SIE platform. This is a systems software role: you will design and write the services that let independent simulators share one world — a common clock, a common entity namespace, and a clear model of who owns what — and the tooling that lets users author, reuse, and debug the scenarios they run.  This is a new area with a wide surface. You will be one of the first engineers on it, which means you will set the technical direction, make the architectural calls, and be accountable for them. Most of your time is spent building, but not all of it: you will periodically work alongside the teams adopting the platform, onboarding Anduril business lines and integrating their simulators with it. Expect ambiguity: the standards in this domain are decades old, the implementations in the wild vary wildly in quality, and the correct design for our constraints is not written down yet. We expect you to work end-to-end — design, implement, ship, operate, and iterate.

  • Make simulation runs deterministic and reproducible enough that a result is evidence, not a demo — including time control, replay, and the instrumentation that explains a divergence
  • Build and generalize the scenario and laydown authoring tooling that engineers and operators use to describe what they want to run
  • Build the content and resource catalogs that let users save, tag, search, and reuse environment and scenario definitions instead of rebuilding them each time
  • Chase down performance: profile hot paths, control allocation and copying, and hold latency and throughput budgets under load with hundreds to thousands of entities
  • Integrate with the rest of the platform — the Go services that provision and schedule compute, the gRPC/protobuf APIs that expose it, and the web UI the team owns
  • Set the technical direction for this area, write the design docs that make it reviewable, and raise the bar through code review and mentorship as the team grows
  • Partner with Anduril business lines when they onboard onto the platform — work alongside their engineers to get their simulators, models, and test workflows integrated, and stay with them until it works in their hands and not just yours
  • Reduce the cost of that onboarding over time by turning the integration work you do by hand into documentation, reference integrations, and SDKs, so the next team can self-serve
  • Work directly with the internal teams and external customers who need this, and convert what they tell you into shipped capability

It connects to live systems, integrates with Anduril's Lattice platform, and runs inside a GUI for interactive scenario authoring.  Mission Sim is a large, mature C++20 codebase with an Entity-Component-System architecture, a stable C ABI plugin system, embedded scripting, and a variety of physics-based models. Keeping this system fast, correct, extensible, and pleasant to develop against at scale, with a growing team of model developers is our job.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Model authoring tools — an early effort you will help stand up to extend the Sim frontend with UI for authoring and tuning Mission Sim models. You will negotiate extension APIs with the GUI team and build an ergonomic UI atop them, working alongside Simulation Modeling engineers.
  • Custom Entity-Component-System architecture that underpins the entire simulator: entity lifecycle, component storage, and the update loop
  • Plugin and SDK development - maintaining a versioned C ABI, which enables external teams to extend the simulator
  • Performance and scale — keeping the simulation loop fast enough for real-time and faster-than-real-time execution with hundreds of concurrent entities; reasoning about memory layout, cache behavior and contention, as entity counts grow
  • Integration architecture — gRPC services, DIS protocol interoperability, networking messaging, and file recording for analysis and playback
  • Support domain experts in integrating new and enhancing existing capability models

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3 years of professional experience with C++20 and strong C++ skills; you should be comfortable with templates, move semantics, smart pointers, and the kinds of design decisions that show up in framework code
  • Experience designing internal APIs and frameworks that other engineers build on, with focus on backwards-compatibility and ergonomics
  • Solid understanding of systems programming fundamentals: memory management, shared libraries, ABI stability, linking, interfacing with the operating system
  • Comfort with linear algebra and applied math
  • Familiarity with Linux-based C++ development toolchains
  • Ability to reason about performance-sensitive code — cache behavior, memory layout, algorithmic complexity
  • Clear technical communication and ability to work in a large, shared codebase and negotiate architectural decisions that affect a growing team
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Government Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of professional experience with C++20
  • Experience leading or mentoring engineers on a project — setting technical direction and bringing others along
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity — scoping the problem, the approach, and the interfaces when none exist yet, and driving them to a decision
  • Experience with military simulation, defense modeling & simulation, or related domains
  • Experience with Entity-Component-System architectures or game engine design patterns
  • Experience in designing and implementing GUI-supported workflows

  • Developing in Nix
  • Experience with numerical simulation, physics modeling, or scientific computing

The Software Platform organization is seeking a Software Engineer to join Anduril’s Tactical Networking Team. We build and operate the Layer 3 networking infrastructure that connects Anduril's autonomous systems and operators across denied, degraded, intermittent, and limited (DDIL) network environments.   • Implement zero-trust identity verification across all mesh communication paths

ABOUT THE JOB

You will own the requirements verification traceability matrix for a maritime autonomous vehicle: the thread that runs from a program requirement, through subsystem allocation, to the specific test or analysis that proves it was met. Reporting to the Systems Engineering, Integration and Test Lead, you keep that thread intact while the design underneath it keeps changing.

By the time this role starts, the requirements baseline and the test campaign will both be in motion. The gap this fills is between them. When a requirement changes, someone has to know which verification items just became invalid; when a test closes, someone has to confirm it actually closed what it claimed. That is this seat.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the requirements verification traceability matrix end to end
  • Maintain allocation from program requirements through subsystem specifications
  • Define verification method for each requirement: test, analysis, inspection, or demonstration
  • Track verification status and report closure against program milestones
  • Run change impact analysis when requirements or interfaces move
  • Write and review requirements for testability, not just correctness
  • Work with the MBSE engineer so traceability lives in the model rather than beside it
  • Work with the T&E Lead so test evidence maps cleanly to verification items
  • Prepare verification artifacts for design reviews and customer milestones
  • Travel up to 15% to test sites and operational locations

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent
  • 7+ years in systems engineering with direct ownership of requirements or verification traceability
  • Experience with requirements management tooling (DOORS, Jama, Polarion, or equivalent)
  • Experience building or maintaining a verification matrix on a hardware program
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with AUV, UUV, submarine, spacecraft, or aircraft programs
  • Experience with MBSE and SysML, particularly requirements traceability inside a model
  • Experience supporting formal verification reviews or customer milestone deliveries
  • Scripting for traceability reporting and data extraction (Python, SQL)
  • Experience on a program where the requirements baseline was still being written

Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance.

We are scaling at an historic pace, anchored by Arsenal-2, our new software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base.

Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. At the same time, it will build the industrial muscle to field our next-generation AUVs at scale.

We aren't waiting for the new shipyard to be completed. The work on this transformation starts right now, with development inside our new 160,000 square foot Proto-Factory in Orange County, California, where the team is already laying the foundation. As the prototyping hub for Arsenal-2, this facility gives us a multi-year head start, proving out the advanced manufacturing methods, digital workflows, and quality systems that will scale across our broader shipyard network.

In Anduril's Maritime Division, we are actively building America's next decisive advantage at sea—and this is the moment to join us.

ABOUT THE JOB

You will own navigation, guidance, and control for a maritime autonomous vehicle. Reporting to the Cognitive Systems Lead, you will lead a team covering inertial navigation, safe navigation systems, and actuation control software. You will define how the vehicle knows where it is, where it needs to go, and how it gets there across GPS-denied ocean environments.

Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own GN&C architecture: inertial navigation, safe navigation, and actuation control software
  • Lead INS integration and GPS-denied navigation solution development
  • Drive Safe Navigation System design and safety certification approach
  • Define actuation and control software requirements in coordination with body subsystem
  • Manage navigation compute requirements and hardware selection
  • Lead trade studies across navigation sensor suites and fusion approaches
  • Lead and mentor IC3/4 engineers across GN&C sub-disciplines
  • Interface with VMS, communications, and mission systems teams
  • Support prototype integration, testing, and sea trials
  • Travel up to 25% to test sites and customer locations
  • Own GN&C architecture: inertial navigation, safe navigation, actuation control software, depth keeping and hover
  • Lead trade studies across navigation sensor suites and fusion approaches, including make vs buy

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or equivalent
  • 8+ years of experience in GN&C, inertial navigation, or vehicle control systems
  • Experience with INS, Kalman filtering, or sensor fusion
  • Familiarity with control system design for marine or aerospace vehicles
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with AUV, UUV, or submarine navigation systems
  • Working knowledge of GPS-denied navigation techniques (DVL, USBL, terrain-aided navigation)
  • Experience with safety-critical navigation system design
  • Familiarity with MATLAB/Simulink or equivalent modeling tools
  • Experience in defense or maritime robotics

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to own execution for the Sand Table team—someone who will maintain our timelines, resolve dependencies, and keep everything on the rails towards final delivery. This is a high-agency role for someone who moves on things before being asked, anticipates problems before they materialize, and drives relentlessly toward outcomes. You will be the connective tissue between design, engineering, product, and key stakeholders, ensuring that our team ships high-quality, consistent releases on cadence while protecting the team's focus and momentum.

You'll manage the full complexity of delivering a real-time 3D platform that spans C++ engine development, XR hardware integration, plugin frameworks, and live demonstrations to senior government and military leaders. This means coordinating across technical work-streams, managing the logistics of high-stakes demos, and ensuring that every release meets the bar our audience demands. You should be comfortable navigating ambiguity, operating with minimal direction, and building the processes and structures that allow a fast-moving team to scale without losing speed.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own execution end-to-end. Drive the team's delivery cadence from planning through release. Maintain timelines, track milestones, and ensure the team consistently hits its commitments. You are the single point of accountability for "are we on track?"
  • Resolve dependencies and remove blockers. Proactively identify cross-team dependencies, external blockers, and resource constraints. Move decisively to resolve them—escalating when necessary, negotiating when possible, and always keeping the team unblocked.
  • Protect the team's time and focus. Clearly articulate blockers, risks, and work in progress to stakeholders so the team can stay heads-down on delivery. Serve as a shield against thrash and scope creep while ensuring legitimate priorities are addressed.
  • Drive high-quality, consistent releases. Help establish and maintain release processes that ensure every build meets quality standards. Coordinate across engineering, QA, and integration efforts to deliver polished, demo-ready software on a reliable cadence.
  • Manage stakeholders and communication. Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders across business development, product, and leadership. Provide clear, concise program updates—surfacing risks early, setting expectations accurately, and translating technical complexity into business-impact language.
  • Coordinate demonstration logistics. Partner with the team to manage the complex logistics of delivering flawless XR demonstrations to critical audiences. Track hardware readiness, software stability, content preparation, and venue requirements to ensure every demo is executed without a hitch.
  • Build and improve processes. Implement lightweight, effective processes for planning, tracking, and delivery that match the team's pace. Leverage tools like Jira or similar to provide visibility without creating overhead. Continuously iterate on what works.
  • Anticipate and mitigate risk. Maintain a living picture of technical, schedule, and integration risks. Develop mitigation plans proactively and adjust course as conditions change—never letting the team be surprised by something that was foreseeable.

  • Demonstrated track record of owning execution for cross-functional technical teams and shipping on-time
  • Strong technical literacy—ability to understand system architecture, software dependencies, build/release pipelines, and technical trade-offs without needing to write the code yourself
  • High agency and intrinsic motivation; you move on problems before being asked and operate effectively with minimal direction
  • Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple parallel work-streams, competing priorities, and shifting timelines
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills—able to build trust, set expectations, and clearly articulate status, risks, and trade-offs to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Experience with project management tooling (Jira, Confluence, Linear, or equivalent) and establishing delivery processes for engineering teams
  • Willingness to travel as needed for demonstrations and events (up to 25%)
  • Must be a U.S. person eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in real-time 3D applications, game engines, XR, or graphics-intensive software development environments
  • Background in defense, aerospace, or national security—understanding of the stakeholder landscape and demonstration culture
  • Experience managing release processes for software with hardware-in-the-loop dependencies (XR headsets, specialized display systems, etc.)
  • Familiarity with C++ development workflows, plugin architectures, or game studio production pipelines
  • Experience coordinating live demonstrations or events with high-profile audiences with high-profile audiences and very-high stakes
  • Track record of building program management processes from scratch in fast-moving, early-stage, or startup environments
  • Experience managing programs with both software delivery and physical logistics components
  • Active U.S. Secret (or higher) security clearance

The goal of a Machine Learning Engineer at Scale is to leverage techniques in the fields of generative AI, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and agentic AI to improve Scale's products and customer experience in production environments. Our machine learning engineers take advantage of robust internal infrastructure and  unique access to massive datasets to deliver improvements to our customers.

Our Public Sector Machine Learning team is focused on deploying cutting-edge models to mission-critical government systems through products like  Donovan and Thunderforge. Our work spans multiple modalities, with a strong focus on both large language models and computer vision. On the LLM side, we are developing agentic systems that help solve complex operational and planning challenges for government partners. This includes building agent frameworks that integrate with custom retrieval pipelines and production APIs, as well as evaluation tools to benchmark and refine agent behavior. We're also advancing research in areas like reinforcement learning for agentic LLMs, with successful deployment into real-world operational environments. On the computer vision front, we're training advanced models to increase labeling throughput and automate perception tasks. Our efforts include building large-scale fine-tuning pipelines, training models across multiple modalities, and developing generalizable vision foundation models to support a wide range of defense applications.

You will:

  • Take state of the art models developed internally and from the community, use them in production to solve problems for our customers and taskers
  • Improve and maintain production models through retraining, hyperparameter tuning, and architectural updates, while preserving core performance characteristics
  • Collaborate with product and research teams to identify and prototype ML-driven product enhancements, including for upcoming product lines
  • Work with massive datasets to develop both generic models as well as fine tune models for specific products
  • Build scalable machine learning infrastructure to automate and optimize our ML services
  • Serve as a cross-functional representative and advocate for machine learning techniques across engineering and product organizations
  • Be comfortable learning new technologies quickly and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Comfortable with light travel (approximately 10%) for customer interaction and team needs

This role will require an active TS security clearance 

Ideally You’d Have:

  • 2+ years of experience building and deploying applied ML systems in production environments
  • Extensive experience with GenAI, Agentic AI, natural language processing, deep learning and deep reinforcement learning, or computer vision in a production environment
  • Solid background in algorithms, data structures, and object-oriented programming
  • Strong programming skills in Python, experience in Tensorflow or PyTorch

  • Experience with geospatial data or maps - GIS tooling, spatial reference systems, or imagery.
  • A shipped project with real users behind it, where you owned it after launch rather than handing it off at merge.

The goal of a Senior Machine Learning Engineer at Scale is to own how we apply generative AI, agentic AI, computer vision, and reinforcement learning to mission-critical problems in production. Our senior machine learning engineers are handed problems that don't yet have an established approach, they propose the architecture, build it with support from other engineers, and are accountable for whether it holds up in the environments our customers depend on.

Our Public Sector Machine Learning team is focused on deploying cutting-edge models to mission-critical government systems through products like Donovan and Thunderforge. Our work spans multiple modalities, with our primary focus on agentic systems built on large language models. We are developing agents that solve complex operational and planning challenges for government partners: agent frameworks that integrate custom retrieval pipelines and production APIs, memory and context-management systems that hold state across long-running tasks, geospatial reasoning over maps and spatial data, and the evaluation tooling that benchmarks and refines agent behavior. We also apply reinforcement learning in targeted places where it earns its keep, and our computer vision work advances evaluation, labeling efficiency, and multimodal model training in support of defense applications.

As a Senior MLE, you'll have design authority over a capability area - the final say on the patterns used within your team, and the responsibility to make those patterns work under real constraints: classified environments, limited compute, and correctness requirements that don't bend.

You will:

  • Own the design and delivery of agent capabilities end to end - architecture, implementation, and the evaluation that proves they work
  • Define net-new patterns in problem spaces with no established approach, propose them to the wider team, and lead the work to build them
  • Take state of the art models developed internally and from the community and put them into production to solve problems for our customers and taskers
  • Improve and maintain production models and agents through retraining, hyperparameter tuning, and architectural updates, while preserving core performance characteristics
  • Build agent-level evaluation benchmarks, LLM judges, and verifiers - and use it to hillclimb performance rather than just report on it
  • Partner with product and research teams to scope and shape high-impact initiatives, including for upcoming product lines
  • Build scalable machine learning infrastructure to automate and optimize our ML services
  • Work directly with government users and subject-matter experts, and translate what you learn into technical direction
  • Act as a force multiplier and a primary reviewer for your team, mentoring at least one engineer, and your manager's go-to on feasibility questions
  • Communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to non-technical stakeholders
  • Treat security and compliance as design constraints to engineer around rather than blockers to route past
  • Serve as a cross-functional representative and advocate for machine learning techniques across engineering and product organizations
  • Be comfortable learning new technologies quickly and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Comfortable with light travel (approximately 10%) for customer interaction and team needs

This role will require an active TS security clearance

Ideally You'd Have:

  • 5+ years of experience building and deploying applied ML systems in production environments
  • Extensive experience with GenAI, Agentic AI, natural language processing, deep learning and deep reinforcement learning, or computer vision in a production environment
  • A track record of owning architectural decisions and defending the tradeoffs behind them - not just implementing a design handed to you
  • Experience shipping agentic systems with real production traffic and evaluation rigor, rather than prototypes or demos
  • Solid background in algorithms, data structures, and object-oriented programming
  • Strong programming skills in Python, experience in PyTorch or Tensorflow
  • Experience mentoring or reviewing the work of other engineers

  • Experience working with cloud platforms (eg. AWS or GCP) and deploying machine learning models in cloud environments
  • Experience with computer vision, generative AI models, large language models, or agentic systems
  • Familiarity with ML evaluation frameworks and agentic model design
  • Experience deploying ML in classified, air-gapped, or IL5+ environments
  • Geospatial or GEOINT experience
  • Inference optimization experience 
  • Fine-tuning experience: SFT, RL, or embedding models

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

The Director, USAF Growth Campaign Leader leads the internal operating rhythm that enables Shield AI’s UAS pursuits with the United States Air Force. Opportunity-focused Go-To-Market (GTM) leaders retain ownership of their customers, capture strategies, account plans, and individual pursuits. This role serves as the connective tissue across those leaders, integrating information across the USAF portfolio and providing the VP, Mission Solutions for the X-BAT FoS with a clear, decision-ready view of campaign health, priorities, dependencies, risks, mitigations, and resource requirements. 

The Director connects USAF pursuits with relevant activity across other Services, allied and partner nations, product and engineering, government approvals, aircraft and test availability, internal investment, and industrial strategy. The role identifies shared dependencies and resource conflicts early, helps sequence competing demands, and coordinates the cross-functional support required for GTM leads to execute their captures effectively. 

The role maintains the authoritative USAF campaign picture and runs the operating cadence that turns portfolio insight into action. This includes campaign reviews, risk and dependency management, executive dashboards, action tracking, investment recommendations, and escalation of decisions requiring VP or executive attention. The Director ensures that information flows efficiently from the GTM organization to the VP, Mission Solutions and that leadership receives clear recommendations rather than unstructured reporting. 

GTM leads remain accountable for customer engagement, account planning, capture strategy, win strategy, price-to-win, proposal content, and pursuit outcomes. The Director enables their success by improving coordination, reducing friction around shared resources, and ensuring that the broader organization is aligned behind the highest-priority USAF opportunities. 

Scope & authority:

    This is a senior, high-visibility seat with authority, not a reporting function: 
  • Portfolio: Concurrent USAF pursuits across the X-BAT FoS, representing a multi-billion-dollar addressable opportunity. 
  • Team: Leadership by influence role, leveraging dedicated capture-operations and analyst support, with the expectation to build the team as the portfolio scales. 
  • Investment: Develops and co-stewards annual campaign and indirect investment against prioritized campaign returns. 
  • Governance: holds a standing seat in USAF bid/no-bid and investment-prioritization reviews and sets the agenda for the executive campaign review. 
  • Growth path: a pipeline role toward senior Department of the Navy growth or general-management leadership at Shield AI. 

What you'll do:

  • Own the USAF view. Build and maintain the integrated USAF campaign picture across all X-BAT FoS USAF pursuits: strategy status, critical path, milestones, dependencies, decision points, and campaign health in one authoritative view. 
  • Enable GTM leads. Give each GTM lead the templates, playbooks, data, competitive inputs, cost and schedule inputs, and cross-functional access they need to build and execute their own capture plan. Success is measured by their outcomes, not by your visibility. 
  • Synchronize functions. Coordinate engineering, product, export, legal, contracts, finance, government relations, and business operations against a single prioritized campaign plan so GTM leads are not individually negotiating for the same scarce resources. 
  • Surface conflicts between campaigns. Identify where two or more campaigns compete for the same aircraft, test window, engineering effort, approval bandwidth, or indirect dollar, and bring executive leadership a clear tradeoff and a recommendation. 
  • Drive executive decision quality. Run the operating cadence — campaign reviews, gate reviews, risk registers, action tracking, and executive dashboards — so leadership receives timely, accurate, decision-ready information on bid/no-bid, investment, and prioritization. 
  • Steward indirect investment. Work with Finance and Business Operations to track campaign investment, indirect spend, and resource planning against campaign priorities and expected return. 
  • Scale discipline. Systematically capture lessons learned across capture efforts—both what worked and what did not, and translate them into repeatable tools, templates, metrics, and playbooks so every new campaign begins with a stronger foundation than the last. 
  • Support a culture of accountability, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 
  • Roll up your sleeves. Personally drive the execution of critical customer responses (RFI, RFP, CSO, and other solicitation vehicles) — assembling cross-functional inputs, holding the response schedule, and driving on-time submission, while the GTM lead retains ownership of win strategy, price-to-win, and proposal content. 

Decision rights & interfaces:

  • This role is accountable for: the integrated USAF campaign plan; the operating cadence and campaign-health reporting; identification and escalation of cross-campaign dependencies, conflicts, and risks; path-to-win roadmap; and recommendations on investment prioritization and sequencing. 
  • Opportunity GTM leads are accountable for: customer relationships and engagement, capture strategy, win strategy and price-to-win for their pursuit, proposal content, and the bid/no-bid recommendation for their opportunity. 
  • Government Relations, Export, Legal, and Contracts are accountable for: data-rights, political and legislative engagements and outcomes, disclosure determinations, legal positions, and contracting terms. 
  • Engineering and Product are accountable for: technical solution definition, configuration decisions, and performance commitments. 
  • Program Management is accountable for: execution of customer-funded programs after award. 
  • External customer engagement by this role is in support of, and at the invitation of, the responsible GTM lead. 

Required qualifications:

  • U.S. person as defined by ITAR (22 CFR 120.62), with the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Top Secret/SCI clearance and Special Access Program (SAP) eligibility. 
  • 12–20+ years in capture management, program management, strategic operations, business operations, technical program management, or a comparable cross-functional leadership role. 
  • Demonstrated success leading highly complex initiatives with multiple interdependent workstreams across engineering, business development, operations, finance, and executive leadership. 
  • Working knowledge of how USAF programs actually get funded and fielded — SAF/AQ and HAF staffing processes, PEO and program-office dynamics, the PPBE/POM cycle, and rapid-acquisition pathways such as OTAs, CSOs, SBIR/STRATFI, AFWERX, and the transition from prototype to program of record. 
  • Proven ability to influence without direct authority and to drive accountability across functions and geographies. 
  • Strong executive communication: leadership briefings, dashboards, metrics, and decision-support materials that lead to decisions rather than discussion. 
  • Deep operational rigor in integrated schedules, critical path, milestones, action tracking, dependency management, and risk mitigation. 
  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-changing environments with competing priorities across multiple time zones. 
  • A service orientation toward the GTM leads this role supports, and the judgment to know when to escalate versus resolve quietly. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Active DoD Top Secret/SCI clearance and current Special Access Program accesses. 
  • Experience supporting DoW, aerospace, autonomy, robotics, aviation, or defense-technology organizations. 
  • Experience within business development, capture, proposal operations, strategic planning, or growth organizations running multiple concurrent U.S. Government pursuits. 
  • Familiarity with the export and international mechanisms that shape USAF pursuits — foreign disclosure determinations, FMS/DCS pathways, and security cooperation planning — where allied demand affects the USAF business case. 
  • Experience building executive dashboards, KPIs, operational scorecards, or portfolio health metrics. 
  • Experience supporting executive staff, chief-of-staff organizations, Strategy and Operations teams, or enterprise PMOs. 
  • Fluency with integrated schedule and work-management tooling (e.g., Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Jira), and an advanced degree or relevant certification (MBA, PMP, Lean Six Sigma) is a plus but not required. 

Success in this role:

  • GTM leads report that the role makes their campaign easier to run, not heavier to report on. 
  • USAF path-to-win is in place and running on a predictable, repeatable cadence that the organization can plan against. 
  • Cross-campaign resource and timing conflicts reach leadership as a decision with a recommendation. 
  • Executive leadership have an accurate health picture of the USAF X-BAT FoS portfolio and make investment calls with confidence. 
  • Campaign mechanisms are reused across opportunities, and each new pursuit stands up measurably faster than the previous one. 

How we work:

    Shield AI’s core values — Do What Honor Dictates, Live as a Servant Leader, and Pursue Excellence — are how we hire, promote, and make hard calls. This role in particular demands servant leadership: success is measured by the outcomes of the GTM leads it supports. 

    Veterans and transitioning service members: we actively seek candidates with U.S. Air Force operational, staff, or acquisition experience, and we support military-to-civilian transitions.

Job Description:

As a Senior Staff (L5) Environmental Control System (ECS) Engineer, you will take full technical ownership of the Environmental Control System architecture, analysis, design, and integration for a dedicated special access program. Serving as the sole ECS subject matter expert on this program, you will work from first principles to execute trades, size systems, design hardware, manage external suppliers, support proposals and capture, and deliver flight-ready hardware in a rapid-iteration development environment.  This position requires a balance of technical rigor, rapid decision-making, and hands-on engineering to efficiently transition concepts into operational capability. The ideal candidate is comfortable solving complex problems, taking ownership, working within an accelerated aircraft development environment, and is motivated by getting meaningful capability into the hands of operators quickly.

What you'll do:

  • Architecture and Trades: Lead ECS architecture definition and trade studies (e.g., vapor cycle vs. air cycle vs. passive/ram-air systems) to meet vehicle thermal, electrical, mass, and volume constraints.
  • Aerothermal and Circuit Design: Design and analyze vehicle air inlets, scoops, ducting networks, and ram-air cooling circuits to ensure adequate flow across flight envelopes.
  • Thermal and Fluid System Sizing: Perform first-principles thermodynamic and heat transfer hand calculations, backed by 1D fluid-thermal network modeling.
  • Component Sourcing and Vendor Management: Author technical specifications and statements of work (SOW) for ECS hardware (heat exchangers, fans, valves, compressors, sensors), evaluate vendors, and drive supplier technical execution.
  • Test and Validation: Define qualification and verification test plans, design test rigs, support instrumentation/DAQ setup, and execute test campaigns to validate performance against requirements.
  • Flight Test and Troubleshooting: Process flight-test thermal and fluid data to identify discrepancies, resolve anomalies via root-cause investigation, and implement rapid design changes.

Required qualifications:

  • Experience: 7 to 12 years of direct experience in aerospace Environmental Control System and vehicle thermal/fluid system development.
  • Education: B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Core Fundamentals: Deep mastery of thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer applied to aircraft or defense systems.
  • Modeling and Analysis: Demonstrated capability with 1D system modeling (e.g., Amesim, Flowmaster, or Python/MATLAB fluid networks) and ability to size systems from inlets to ram circuits to liquid cooling systems, air cooling systems, and more.
  • CAD and PLM: Experience in 3D CAD modeling, routing, and drawing release (Siemens NX preferred, or equivalent like CATIA/Creo) with PLM workflows.
  • Hardware and Supplier Execution: Proven track record sourcing COTS/custom aerospace components, driving suppliers to schedule, and assembling benchtop or vehicle-level test setups.
  • Autonomy: Demonstrated ability to self-direct, prioritize technical tasks without oversight, and deliver functional hardware under tight timelines.
  • Clearance eligible

Preferred qualifications:

  • Familiarity with aerospace environmental requirements and test standards (e.g., MIL-STD-810, MIL-HDBK-310, RTCA DO-160, SAE AIR/ARP standards).

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Staff Aerostructures Design Engineer to support the development of structural components for our next-generation autonomous aircraft. As a key contributor on the team, you will design and develop high-performance structural components from concept through production release.

You’ll work cross-functionally to ensure structural integrity, manufacturability, and system integration across one of the most advanced autonomous aircraft platforms being built today. This role is ideal for an aerospace mechanical engineer who thrives in hands-on design environments and is eager to take increasing ownership of flight-critical designs.

What you'll do:

  • Design and develop structural components and assemblies for Shield AI’s next-generation UAV platform.
  • Execute all stages of the design lifecycle including conceptual development, initial CAD modeling, detailed design, and drawing release.
  • Perform hand calculations for stress or strain with limited basic FEA analysis, with guidance from senior engineers as needed.
  • Collaborate closely with aerodynamics, propulsion, avionics, payload, and manufacturing teams to support system integration across airframe interfaces.
  • Support structural validation efforts including coupon testing, subcomponent testing, and system-level verification.
  • Generate high-quality design documentation, drawings, interface definitions, and analysis reports in compliance with aerospace standards.
  • Partner with manufacturing and flight test teams to resolve build issues and support hardware through test and deployment.
  • Participate in design reviews and technical discussions, presenting work clearly and incorporating feedback effectively.
  • Continuously improve personal technical depth in structural layout, joints, fasteners, tolerancing, and structural optimization.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or related discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience in aircraft structural design or closely related aerospace structures.
  • Experience designing and releasing structural components in development or production environments.
  • Working knowledge of composite and metallic structures, including fasteners, bonded joints, and load paths.
  • Proficiency in CAD tools (NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or similar).
  • Understanding of GD&T, tolerance stackups, and DFMA principles.
  • Strong written and verbal technical communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate in fast-paced, high-ownership engineering environments

Preferred qualifications:

  • M.S. degree in Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering.
  • Experience supporting UAV, DoD, or aerospace vehicle programs.
  • Familiarity with aerospace standards (MIL-STD, ASME Y14.5, FAA).
  • Experience supporting hardware through test, failure analysis, and design iteration.
  • Exposure to composite design and manufacturing methods.
  • Experience using FEA tools (ANSYS, Abaqus, NASTRAN, or similar) for linear structural analysis

As a Staff (L4) Aircraft Thermal Systems Engineer, you will take full technical ownership of thermal analysis, design, and vehicle integration for a Group 5 UAV fighter aircraft. You will work from first principles to characterize aircraft-level thermal environments, evaluate heat-transfer pathways, develop cooling solutions, correlate analytical and computational models, and deliver robust thermal systems and hardware in a rapid-iteration development environment. This position requires a balance of technical rigor, rapid decision-making, and hands-on engineering to efficiently transition concepts into operational capability. The ideal candidate is comfortable solving complex problems, taking ownership, working within an accelerated aircraft development environment, and is motivated by getting meaningful capability into the hands of operators quickly.

  • Thermal Analysis and Modeling: Perform first-principles heat transfer and fluid mechanics calculations, then develop analytical, finite-difference, and CFD models to characterize conduction, convection, radiation, and coupled thermal-fluid behavior.
  • Cooling System Design: Design and evaluate active and passive cooling solutions, including heat-rejection paths, airflow, ducting, thermal interfaces, and hardware needed to manage vehicle thermal loads.
  • Requirements and Risk Management: Generate thermal requirements, assess technical risks, and develop actionable design recommendations that balance thermal performance with vehicle power, mass, volume, maintainability, and integration constraints.
  • Vehicle and Hardware Integration: Develop thermal hardware layouts and CAD models, and resolve interfaces with structures, avionics, fluid systems, EWIS, and adjacent mechanical systems.
  • Test and Validation: Define qualification and verification test plans, design test rigs, support instrumentation and data acquisition, and correlate analytical and computational models with test data.
  • Hardware and Supplier Execution: Author technical specifications and statements of work for thermal hardware, evaluate suppliers, and drive supplier technical execution through prototype build and test.
  • Qualification and Hardware Delivery: Define and execute qualification test plans per MIL-STD-810, using results to mature the design into production-ready hardware and support MIL-HDBK-516 Airworthiness Certification.
  • Technical Leadership: Communicate thermal findings through design reviews and technical reports, guide cross-disciplinary teams in applying thermal and fluid fundamentals, and influence vehicle-level thermal design decisions.

Required qualifications:

  • Clearance required: US Citizens Only & Must have an Active Secret or higher clearance.
  • Experience: 7 to 12 years of direct experience in aerospace thermal engineering, environmental control systems, or vehicle thermal and fluid system development.
  • Education: B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Core Fundamentals: Deep mastery of thermodynamics, heat transfer, and fluid dynamics applied to aircraft or defense systems.
  • Modeling and Analysis: Demonstrated capability with first-principles hand calculations, finite-difference methods, and CFD or thermal-analysis tools such as FloEFD, STAR-CCM+, Thermal Desktop, or equivalent.
  • Thermal System Design: Demonstrated ability to design active and passive cooling solutions and manage thermal environments for aircraft bays, engine bays, hot surfaces, or comparable aerospace installations.
  • CAD and PLM: Experience in 3D CAD modeling, thermal hardware layout, routing, and drawing release with Siemens NX, CATIA, Creo, SolidWorks, or equivalent PLM workflows.
  • Hardware and Supplier Execution: Proven track record sourcing COTS/custom aerospace components, driving suppliers to schedule, and assembling benchtop or vehicle-level test setups.
  • Autonomy: Demonstrated ability to self-direct, prioritize technical tasks without oversight, and deliver functional hardware under tight timelines.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with high-altitude aircraft thermal management, analysis, and design.
  • Hands-on experience with thermal and fluid system testing, instrumentation, data acquisition, and validation.
  • Knowledge of materials and manufacturing methods relevant to aerospace thermal management.
  • Background in multi-disciplinary system integration spanning avionics, fluid systems, and systems engineering.
  • Familiarity with aerospace environmental and airworthiness requirements and test standards, including MIL-STD-810, MIL-HDBK-310, RTCA DO-160, and SAE AIR or ARP standards.
