We are looking for the founding members of this new business area for Netflix.

The Identity & Signals team builds the identity foundation of the Netflix ads business — the graph and matching systems that let us recognize the same person or household across signals, devices, and partner data sources, and that determine which signals we can responsibly and accurately use for targeting, measurement, and reporting. We build and maintain the identity graph, run and evaluate entity-matching and resolution pipelines, and manage relationships with identity providers so that advertisers and internal teams can trust the signals underneath every campaign.

This is a foundational role on a small, high-leverage team. You will build the analytics and data infrastructure that powers identity matching and graph construction — designing the tables, pipelines, and metrics that let the team and its stakeholders understand match quality, coverage, and drift over time. You'll work end-to-end: from raw signal ingestion, through matching logic and graph construction, to the dashboards and data products that make identity health visible and actionable across the company.

In This Role, You Will

  • Design, build, and maintain the data models and pipelines that support identity graph construction, entity matching, and identity resolution across first-party and third-party signals.
  • Partner with data engineering and software engineering to productionize matching logic, ensuring pipelines are scalable, well-tested, and monitored for data quality and drift.
  • Build metrics, dashboards, and analytics that quantify match rate, match quality, coverage, and graph stability, and that surface anomalies before they affect downstream campaigns.
  • Work closely with data science to evaluate and improve matching algorithms, providing the clean, well-documented data and features needed to test and iterate on models.
  • Manage and evaluate the analytics relationship with external identity providers (e.g., Experian, TransUnion, LiveRamp), including onboarding new sources, validating match performance, and monitoring ongoing data quality.
  • Translate identity graph and matching concepts — nodes, edges, match confidence, deterministic vs. probabilistic matching — into clear, actionable insights for product, sales, and other non-technical stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with product and cross-functional partners to define identity requirements, evaluate trade-offs (accuracy vs. coverage vs. privacy), and prioritize roadmap work.
  • Communicate technical decisions, trade-offs, and results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences at all levels of the company.

We Are Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience as an analytics engineer, data engineer, or similar role working with large-scale data.
  • Experience working with graph data structures and graph-based data models (e.g., property graphs, graph databases, or graph analytics on top of relational/columnar stores).
  • Familiarity with entity matching / identity resolution concepts — deterministic and probabilistic matching, fuzzy matching, blocking/candidate generation, and match quality evaluation.
  • Knowledge of, or direct experience working with, identity providers such as Experian, TransUnion, LiveRamp, or similar data/identity partners.
  • Strong SQL and Python skills, with experience building and maintaining production data pipelines.
  • Experience designing data models, metrics, and dashboards that make complex technical systems understandable to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate closely across data engineering, software engineering, data science, and product teams.
  • Ability to work independently, drive your own projects, and make compelling cases for prioritization.
  • Embodies the Netflix values while bringing a new perspective to continue improving our culture.

Nice To Have

  • Experience with ad-tech identity concepts — cross-device identity, household graphs, cookie/ID deprecation, or media measurement.
  • Experience with graph databases or graph-processing frameworks (e.g., Neo4j, Neptune, GraphFrames, or similar).
  • Familiarity with our ML/data stack (Metaflow) or comparable large-scale data tooling.
  • Experience working with privacy-sensitive data and an understanding of relevant data governance and privacy considerations for identity data.
  • Experience applying GenAI to boost developer/analytics productivity.

Great recommendations are how members find something worth their time. We are looking for an experienced Human Evaluations Program Manager to help us measure and improve the quality of recommendations across the Netflix homepage and discovery experience. You will work alongside Product Management and ML teams to build the human evaluation programs that tell us whether recommendations are working for members, and where they are not.

About the Role

Netflix is building toward more relevant, more varied, and more trustworthy recommendations, and thoughtful, high-quality evaluation is essential to making sure we are moving in the right direction. Join a team creating the frameworks, tools, and workflows that ensure human judgment is applied with consistency, clarity, and care, whether we are evaluating relevance, repetition, diversity, or whether a recommendation simply makes sense to the member.

You will not only shape how human evaluations of our recommendations are designed, but also own the day-to-day execution. From scoping and planning to vendor management, rater onboarding, and calibration, you will be accountable for driving delivery from start to finish. Just as critically, you will act as a thought partner to Product Management, helping translate recommendation strategy into evaluation designs and building a shared language around recommendation quality across teams.

The Opportunity

In this role, you will partner across product, research, data science, UX, and engineering to develop rubrics, frameworks, and workflows that enable rigorous, scalable human evaluation of recommendations. Beyond shaping the "what" and "how," you will also lead the "when" and "done." You will keep evaluation projects on track, ensuring consistent execution, timely delivery, efficient use of vendor capacity, and high rater alignment. If you are excited to bring structure to ambiguity and influence what members see when they open Netflix, while being accountable for tangible delivery, this is your chance to create meaningful impact from day one.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate brings a rare combination of structure and flexibility. You know how to create evaluation frameworks that are rigorous and scalable, and you are also a driver who gets them out the door. You are skilled at translating product strategy into evaluation workflows, defining milestones, managing vendors, and delivering consistent results in a dynamic environment. You can steer teams across functions, keep timelines on track, and ensure rater quality without micromanaging. You are curious about how personalization works and can build credibility with PMs, data scientists, and ML engineers. You have working fluency in film and TV content and can quickly scan a set of titles to tell whether they belong together. You thrive in spaces where there is no roadmap, and you take pride in making things real, not just possible.

  • Lead end-to-end execution of human evaluation and data operations initiatives, from intake and scoping to delivery

  • Manage human annotation vendors, including capacity planning, SLAs, quality performance, and escalations
  • Drive operational efficiency across evaluation programs, including cost per task, throughput, turnaround time, and speed to IRR
  • Develop clear, scalable guidelines and scoring rubrics to ensure consistent rater judgment, including for subjective, taste-based questions
  • Oversee rater onboarding, calibration, and QA workflows
  • Pilot and refine evaluation tasks to improve clarity, inter-rater reliability, and feedback quality
  • Anticipate and resolve bottlenecks and blockers
  • Act as the connective tissue across product, ML, data science, and vendor partners to ensure alignment and effective execution of evaluations at scale

Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience working in human evaluations, data collection, labeling, or annotation operations in ML environments
  • Track record of implementing process improvements or quality control systems for data collection needs
  • Prior experience managing human annotation vendors, raters, or data labeling teams, including vendor performance and cost management
  • Experience improving operational efficiency of annotation programs (throughput, turnaround, cost)
  • Strong understanding of evaluation design, including guidelines, rubrics, and scoring protocols
  • Working fluency in film and TV content, including genres, formats, and talent
  • Proven ability in end-to-end management of complex, cross-functional programs, demonstrating strong Program Management skills and clear accountability for successful delivery
  • Experience with human labeling platforms
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to synthesize feedback into clear recommendations and process improvements
  • Familiarity with how rater subjectivity and bias affect taste-based judgments, and how to account for them in evaluation design
  • Strong organizational skills and executional focus; ability to track details while seeing the bigger picture

Nice To Have

  • Experience with personalization, recommender systems, search, or ranking evaluation
  • Familiarity with how offline human evaluation complements online experimentation (A/B tests) and engagement metrics
  • Experience evaluating at the list or page level, not only the individual item level
  • Experience partnering with Product Managers and Data Scientists on metric definition

Securing NVIDIA's EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying a standard security stack. The workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for an off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply. That constraint is the job. You'll be an individual contributor on Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters, the team that implements security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA's hardware engineers design silicon on - spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud. You will sit alongside the engineers who run these clusters 24x7, close enough to deploy a control, investigate a behavior, and change the running environment yourself.


This is hands-on build work, not control review. You'll decide where conventional tooling applies, where it actively cannot, and then engineer the alternative. If your depth is in large-scale compute, networking, or storage infrastructure at a hyperscaler, a security product company, or anywhere fleets and fabrics are the day job, and you've carried real accountability for the security properties of those systems, you're who we want to talk to. We don't expect fluency in every security product category. We expect you to own outcomes and pick up the remaining domain breadth fast. Security engineering here is engineering: code, instrumentation, and secure-by-default infrastructure - not tickets, exceptions, and spreadsheets.


What You'll Be Doing:

  • Build and operate security controls and telemetry for EDA compute, storage, and networking - design, ship to production, then own them.
  • Engineer around hard constraints. Protect multi-day, high-value compute jobs without degrading them. Where heavyweight in-node agents are not viable, build the workable answer instead.
  • Make the network and platform the control plane. Protection can't depend solely on what runs inside the node.
  • Instrument for detection. Collect and normalize security signals from the fleet into our SIEM, and build the detections and dashboards that turn it into something actionable. Log collection alone is not monitoring.
  • Investigate and respond. Chase down EDA-specific threats and exposure, and execute containment and remediation hands-on with infrastructure and service owners.
  • Automate enforcement and evidence. Infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code so secure configuration is the default state, with compliance evidence produced as an engineering output rather than a manual exercise.
  • Run the lifecycle of the security technologies you own: selection, rollout, operation, and eventual replacement.
  • Work across boundaries. Partner directly with data center operations, IT storage and networking, network engineering, CSP teams, and NVIDIA's central security organization on shared outcomes.
  • Think like an adversary. Threat modeling and mitigation planning across network, storage, and compute.

What We Need To See:

  • 8+ years of hands-on infrastructure or infrastructure-security engineering across on-prem and cloud environments.
  • Strong Linux depth - you are comfortable at the system level, not just the console level.
  • Real experience operating or securing compute fleets at scale: provisioning, lifecycle, and the operational realities of long-running jobs.
  • Working networking expertise applied to large compute environments.
  • Programming/scripting fluency (Python, Go, or shell) used for automation, detection, and tooling you've shipped and maintained.
  • Solid foundations in access control, authentication, segmentation, encryption, and vulnerability lifecycle.
  • A track record of landing changes with partners who don't report to you.
  • Clear written and verbal communication - credible with individual engineers and with leadership.

Microsoft’s Discovery and Quantum (MDQ) division develops and delivers advanced artificial intelligence (AI), cloud-enabled capabilities, and strategic technologies to help solve the world’s major challenges.  From accelerating scientific discovery with advanced AI tools, to pioneering breakthroughs in quantum computing, to advancing robotics and AI capabilities that drive real-world impact, joining MDQ means building the future, partnering with fast-moving innovators, and operating in a high-impact, mission-driven environment. 

At Microsoft Robotics within MDQ, we build and deploy technologies that enable people, robots, and AI agents to collaborate and achieve more. 

We are building Microsoft’s platform for physical intelligence—an integrated robotics software and AI platform that brings together humans, robots, and agents through robotics AI models, innovative teaming solutions and experiences, physically grounded agentic AI workflows, trustworthy test and evaluation, and real-world customer-focused validation. Built on Microsoft’s core platforms and delivered through and with a global ecosystem of partners and customers, this platform accelerates AI for the physical world and helps robotics solutions move from experimentation to reliable, scaled deployment. 

We are hiring a Member of Technical Staff to contribute to the design, development, and testing of core infrastructure components of the Microsoft Robotics platform, including the Software Development Kits (SDKs), cloud services, edge runtimes, developer tooling, and agent orchestration layers that enable people, AI agents, and robots to operate together across end-to-end mission workflows. In this role, you will build well-scoped features with guidance from experienced engineers, explore design options, and develop your skills in robotics software systems while helping bring autonomy capabilities to life. 



Responsibilities

  • Implement and test features within core platform components with guidance, including robotics SDKs, cloud-hosted Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), edge runtimes, and agent orchestration frameworks that enable developers and partners to compose interoperable autonomy capabilities (perception, planning, control, multi-agent coordination) into deployable mission workflows. 

  • Contribute to platform extensibility and integration features using established patterns, helping integrate, version, test, and deploy first-party autonomy capabilities, first- and third-party models, partner hardware systems, and customer-specific logic across cloud and edge environments.

Help test and investigate performance against the latency requirements of real-time robotic control loops.

  • Master's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field with proven experience coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python

Overview

At Microsoft Quantum, we aim to empower science and scientists to solve the world’s biggest problems by realizing advanced computing platforms at the intersection of high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, and quantum information technology. Microsoft Quantum will change the world of computing and help solve some of humankind’s currently unsolvable problems. For more information about our team, visit https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/quantum.

The Cryomechanical team enables Microsoft Quantum’s hardware roadmap by designing, integrating, and sustaining cryogenic mechanical systems, packaging solutions, and laboratory infrastructure that support reliable experimentation, scalable system integration, and disciplined transition from research concepts to producible hardware.

As a Simulation Engineer – Mechanical & Thermal Systems, you will lead mechanical, structural, thermal, and coupled multiphysics analysis for cryogenic hardware and laboratory systems using COMSOL Multiphysics and ANSYS. You will translate system requirements and design concepts into verified computational models, quantify margins and sensitivities, correlate predictions with test data, and deliver clear engineering recommendations that guide architecture, detailed design, manufacturing, integration, and root-cause investigations throughout the product lifecycle.

Microsoft’s culture is grounded in a growth mindset, customer obsession, diversity and inclusion, one Microsoft collaboration, and making a difference through technology. In this role, you will be expected to model these values by learning continuously, partnering across disciplines, communicating clearly, and creating an inclusive environment where rigorous engineering and shared accountability help the team deliver meaningful impact.



Responsibilities
  • Own end-to-end mechanical and thermal analysis for cryogenic subassemblies and top-level integrations, including millikelvin (mK), 4 kelvin (4 K), and ambient-temperature structures, radiation shields, vacuum interfaces, thermal straps, supports, and cable or harness routing hardware.
  • Develop and maintain high-fidelity finite element and multiphysics models in COMSOL Multiphysics and ANSYS Mechanical, including defensible geometry idealization, material models, contacts, interfaces, meshing strategies, loads, boundary conditions, solver controls, and post-processing methods.
  • Perform structural, thermal, and coupled thermo-mechanical analyses, including linear and nonlinear stress, stiffness, deflection, buckling, modal and vibration response, steady-state and transient heat transfer, thermal contact resistance, radiation, and thermal stress caused by coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch.
  • Translate system and subsystem requirements into analysis plans and acceptance criteria for heat-load budgets, temperature stability, thermal anchoring, structural margins, alignment, vacuum loading, vibration isolation, interface loads, and performance across temperature stages.
  • Verify, validate, and correlate simulation results through mesh-convergence studies, sensitivity and uncertainty analyses, hand calculations, analytical benchmarks, and comparison with instrumentation, prototype, and system-level test data.
  • Drive design decisions through clear technical communication by presenting assumptions, methods, limitations, margins, risks, and recommendations at design reviews; partner with mechanical designers, thermal engineers, physicists, electrical engineers, manufacturing teams, and suppliers to close issues and improve designs.
  • Build reusable simulation capability and engineering discipline by creating model templates, material-property libraries, documented workflows, review checklists, and automation for parametric studies and results processing; support root-cause investigations
  • Other:

    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Physics, Engineering, or related field AND 6+ years experience in industry or in a research and development environment

  • 3+ years of experience performing mechanical, structural, thermal, or coupled multiphysics simulation for complex hardware systems, ideally spanning cryogenic through ambient-temperature operation.
  • 3+ years of advanced experience using ANSYS Mechanical and COMSOL Multiphysics for steady-state and transient thermal analysis, nonlinear structural analysis, contact, modal response, vibration, and coupled thermo-mechanical simulation.
  • Experience modeling cryogenic systems and low-temperature hardware, including temperature-dependent material properties, thermal contraction, thermal contact conductance, conductive and radiative heat transfer, heat-load budgets, and thermal anchoring.
  • Experience correlating simulation predictions with test data using temperature sensors, strain or displacement measurements, vibration data, or other instrumentation; ability to identify discrepancies and improve model fidelity.
  • Experience with parametric studies, design optimization, uncertainty quantification, surrogate modeling, or automation using MATLAB, Python, APDL, Java, or comparable scripting and application interfaces.
  • Experience working with CAD and product-development toolchains, including geometry preparation, defeaturing, material and configuration control, and collaboration with design, manufacturing, test, and supplier teams.
  • Experience contributing to inclusive, cross-disciplinary engineering teams by communicating decisions clearly, inviting diverse perspectives, mentoring others in simulation practices, and helping create an environment where team members can contribute effectively and succeed.
  • Advanced experience with COMSOL Multiphysics and/or ANSYS Mechanical, including independent model setup, solution, convergence assessment, results interpretation, and technical documentation for mechanical and thermal systems.
  • Deep foundation in finite element analysis and engineering mechanics, including solid mechanics, heat transfer, materials behavior, numerical methods, contact, and coupled thermal-structural response.

Overview

The Online Forensics team sits within the Microsoft AI Experiences organization, where we protect the monetization network that funds the products people use every day. Because attackers adapt quickly, effective defense requires discovering how systems can be abused, not just investigating known incidents. We combine hands-on adversarial research, controlled experimentation, and large-scale data analysis to establish authoritative ground truth and expose weaknesses before they are exploited at scale. 

As a Principal Applied Scientist, you will discover how web-based monetization systems can be manipulated and build the experimental and investigation systems needed to study that abuse at scale. Your research will cover both exploitable weaknesses and abuse of intended functionality, including automation, identity and attribution manipulation, and multi-step economic exploitation. You will personally write code, construct safe adversarial experiments, and combine experimental evidence with large-scale telemetry to establish mechanism, prevalence, and impact. 

The scientific challenge is to distinguish adversarial manipulation from legitimate behavior under incomplete and potentially manipulated telemetry. You will develop methods to test competing explanations, determine whether experimental findings generalize to real-world traffic, and evaluate candidate signals without unacceptable false positives. You will turn validated approaches into reliable, reusable systems and evaluation methods that partner defense teams can adopt. 

You will own a focused portfolio of high-impact research problems, from hypothesis through implementation, validation, and adoption. At the principal level, you will set scientific and technical direction while remaining directly involved in coding, experimentation, debugging, and delivery. Responsibilities

Datacenter Operations

  • Complies with Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines with guidance from experienced technicians and/or direct-line management. Escalates issues related to compliance or operational assurance activities to direct-line management.
  • Reviews Process Change Notifications (PCNs) and develops an understanding of the impact to work execution and awareness to changes within their area of work and/or the work of others. Asks questions when they do not have required information and may provide feedback on changes to processes to experienced technicians and/or direct-line management.
  • Completes assigned tickets efficiently and in alignment with relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type with guidance from experienced technicians. Seeks guidance from more experienced technicians on challenging or complex tickets.
  • Receives guidance and supervision to develop an understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning IT datacenter technology(ies) and equipment. Datacenter Work Environment
  • Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies with guidance from other technicians.   • Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

Overview

The Agent 365 Foundation team builds and operates the platform layer that keeps agent workloads reliable, secure, and fast at Microsoft scale. Our charter within this group is traffic ingress: every request that reaches our clusters passes through the gateway and edge systems we own. We are the front door, which means we are also the first line of defense and the first place a problem shows up. 

A significant part of our current focus is ingress for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform traffic. That work spans routing and gateway policy, connection and protocol handling, tenant isolation, throttling and abuse mitigation, failover behavior across regions, and the observability needed to reason about all of it while it is happening. The scale is large, the traffic patterns are diverse, and the correctness bar is high. 

About the Role 

We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to design, build, and operate the gateway and ingress path end to end. This is a hands-on engineering role. You will spend your time in code, in design reviews, and in production — writing services in C# and Go, tuning TLS and HTTP/2 behavior, shaping how gRPC traffic flows through the stack, working with Azure Front Door and our own edge components, and hardening the system against volumetric and application-layer attacks. 

You will own outcomes rather than tickets. That means choosing where resiliency belongs in the request path, deciding what a safe failure mode looks like for a given class of traffic, and defending those decisions with data. You will also be part of the on-call rotation for the systems you build, because the fastest way to build a resilient front door is to feel it when it bends. 

Who Thrives in This Role 

The engineer who does well here is genuinely hands-on. You are comfortable being the person who reads the proxy source, reproduces the failure locally, and lands the fix — seniority here means more time close to the system, not less. You think critically about problems before reaching for a solution, ask what the data actually shows, and are willing to challenge a design, including your own, when the evidence points elsewhere. 

You also do not shy away from hard problems. Ambiguous incidents, legacy traffic paths, unfamiliar protocol behavior, and difficult cross-team conversations are part of the work, and you move toward them rather than around them. You are direct, collaborative, and comfortable operating with a high degree of ownership. 

Why This Role Matters 

Ingress is where reliability and security are decided for everything behind it. The work you do here is visible in the availability numbers of some of Microsoft's largest business platforms, and it is felt immediately by the customers who depend on them. If you want a role where deep networking expertise, sound judgment, and engineering craft compound into real impact, this is it. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

  • Design, implement, and operate L4 and L7 ingress components — gateways, proxies, load balancing and routing policy — that carry Dynamics 365 and Power Platform traffic into our clusters. 

  • Own the protocol layer: TLS termination and certificate lifecycle, HTTP/2 connection management, gRPC routing and streaming behavior, and the performance characteristics of each. 

  • Build resiliency into the request path through health-based routing, retries and hedging, circuit breaking, load shedding, rate limiting, and regional failover, and prove the behavior through fault injection and load testing. 

  • Strengthen the security posture of the edge, including DDoS detection and mitigation, WAF and abuse-mitigation policy, tenant isolation, and defense against application-layer attack patterns. 

  • Integrate and tune Azure Front Door and related edge services alongside our first-party gateway components, and make deliberate decisions about which layer solves which problem. 

  • Instrument the ingress path so that latency, error, and saturation questions can be answered in minutes, and drive incident response, root-cause analysis, and the follow-through that keeps the same failure from repeating. 

  • Partner with service teams across Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and Agent 365 on onboarding, capacity, and traffic-shaping decisions, and raise the engineering bar through design and code review. 



Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 4+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python
    • OR equivalent experience.

 Other Requirements:

Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 6+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 8+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python 
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • Proven knowledge of L4 and L7 networking: TCP connection behavior, load balancing, proxying, routing, DNS, and the tradeoffs between transport-level and application-level handling.
  • Practical depth in TLS, HTTP/2, and gRPC, including certificate management, handshake and connection tuning, multiplexing behavior, and diagnosing protocol-level failures from packet captures and traces.
  • Production experience with C# or Go, and the willingness to work fluently in both.
  • Demonstrated experience making services resilient under stress — designing for graceful degradation, and validating it rather than assuming it.
  • Experience operating what you build, including on-call ownership, live-site debugging, and post-incident improvement.
  • Hands-on experience with Azure Front Door, Azure networking, or comparable CDN and global edge platforms.
  • Direct experience with DDoS protection: volumetric and application-layer attack detection, mitigation policy, rate limiting, and bot management.
  • Experience running ingress in Kubernetes environments, including service mesh and Envoy-based data planes.
  • Familiarity with multi-tenant SaaS traffic patterns, such as those in Dynamics 365 or Power Platform, and the isolation and fairness problems they create.
  • Background in performance analysis and capacity planning for high-throughput, low-latency systems.

The Cryomechanical team enables Microsoft Quantum’s hardware roadmap by designing, integrating, and sustaining cryogenic mechanical systems, packaging solutions, and laboratory infrastructure that support reliable experimentation, scalable system integration, and disciplined transition from research concepts to producible hardware.

As a Mechanical Designer – Cryomechanical Systems You will own products from cradle to grave, working hands on to oversee initial builds, incorporating customer feedback to make improvements and driving continuous improvements to equipment as the state-of-the-art advances. You help shape requirements, create complete three-dimensional (3D) models from scratch, produce two-dimensional (2D) drawings, document Bill of Materials (BOM), create standard operating procedures (SOPs) and work hands on in installations to guide products through their entire lifecycle.

Do you love building elegant systems that make engineering teams measurably better? Do you like transforming complex data into actionable insights? Are you passionate about applying software engineering rigor to the measurement and optimization of the development lifecycle itself? As part of our Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) team, you'll architect and engineer a comprehensive telemetry and analytics platform that provides deep telemetry across the entire software development lifecycle. Your work will empower engineering teams across Apple to quantify their performance, identify bottlenecks through engineered observability, and continuously improve their development workflows.

Description

We are seeking an experienced Software Architect or Senior Software Engineer with a strong data analytics background in building data-intensive systems to join our team. The ideal candidate brings production-grade software engineering discipline to data systems — Architecting data models for our scalable SDLC event platform that serves as the backbone for data pipelines, and engineering scalable data infrastructure and analytics capabilities across one of the world's largest software organizations.

Modern software development at Apple spans multiple specialized platforms — source control, build system, deployment orchestration, artifact management, and observability tooling. Each generates rich telemetry, but analyzing these signals in isolation yields limited insight. You'll solve this by engineering a unified analytics platform that correlates events across the entire development pipeline, turning fragmented data into a coherent picture of engineering effectiveness.

Responsibilities

Data Model & Schema Engineering: Engineer unified schemas representing SDLC entities and events across all platforms. Define and standardize event contracts using Apple's CDEvents specification, model relationships between applications, services, deployments, and incidents, and architect a data model that cleanly supports both real-time streaming and batch analytics workloads.
SDLC Platform Integrations: Design for fault tolerance, and schema evolution. Design, build, and own data pipelines that reliably ingest events from source control, build systems, deployment services, test platforms, artifact registries, and monitoring systems. Leverage the CDEvents Platform architecture for event ingestion, implement robust validation and enrichment pipelines, and handle both real-time streaming (Kafka) and API-based data access patterns with production-quality reliability and observability.

Description

Responsibilities

Translate cellular system-level and performance requirements into requirements for the TX line-up and features of RF front-end components, transceiver, and system firmware.

Familiarity with RF systems, front-end (power amplifier, filters, switches, power management), and transceiver architecture, including lineup design and trade-offs (e.g. gain, linearity, noise, power, thermal).

Strong analytical skills, proactive user of AI tools, and ability to collaborate and communicate across multicultural, global teams.

RF front-end and RFIC system modeling and simulation.
Expertise in RF front-end architectures, technologies, and design.

Description

The Maintenance Mechanic – Plumber maintains and repairs the facility's plumbing systems, equipment, and related infrastructure. This role does skilled trades work, including installing, repairing, and altering piping, fixtures, and plumbing equipment. It keeps domestic water, wastewater, and other critical building systems running reliably. As a Maintenance Mechanic – Plumber, you will keep these systems working at their best by finding issues and fixing them. You will work closely with other Places teams, such as Project Management, to maintain our high standards as new infrastructure comes online.

Responsibilities

Maintain and repair domestic water and wastewater systems, including sanitary, storm, and vent piping
Service, repair, and replace plumbing fixtures, flush valves, faucets, drinking fountains, and bottle fillers
Maintain pumps (booster, sump, and sewage ejector), water heaters, boilers, and mixing valves
Inspect, test, and maintain backflow prevention assemblies and water protection systems
Support site utilities, commercial docks, site recycling equipment, and their subsystems
Inspect building infrastructure and equipment on a regular schedule to find leaks, wear, or code issues
Open, assign, complete, and close out work orders in the CMMS for all assigned work
Monitor and respond to plumbing-related alarms in the site's Building Management System (BMS)
Monitor and analyze system data, such as water usage, pressures, and temperatures, to recommend improvements
Take part in major projects, complete some individual projects, and coordinate outside contractors so work is done on time and done correctly
Order parts and materials for projects and repairs
Complete other projects and tasks as assigned
Participate in after-hours on-call rotation to respond to emergencies

High school diploma or GED
Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience in commercial or industrial plumbing maintenance, or in a related trade or technical service environment
Working knowledge of the Uniform Plumbing Code (UPC) and local code requirements
Skilled with soldering, brazing, press fittings, threading, and drain-clearing equipment
Able to read and interpret blueprints, drawings, as-builts, and rough sketches
Experience working with a CMMS; familiarity with a BMS
Strong troubleshooting and customer service skills
Comfortable working from ladders, in mechanical rooms, in crawlspaces, and above ceilings

Preferred Qualifications

Associate's degree in a related field from an accredited institution (five years of related work experience may substitute)
Backflow Prevention Assembly Tester (BPAT) certification
Journeyman Plumber license
Cross-training in HVAC, boilers, or general building maintenance
OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification

ACOS is Apple's geo-distributed, exabyte-scale object storage service. It serves billions of requests per day for iCloud, Apple Music, Apple TV, Apple Maps, and Apple's internal data and analytics platforms. It provides 11-nines of durability and 4-nines of availability.

The ACOS Storage Infrastructure team owns how data is encoded, placed, verified, repaired, and reclaimed inside a storage cluster. This includes erasure and replicated encoding schemes, data placement and rebalancing optimization, compaction, scrubbing and repair, durability modeling, performance tiering, and the supply chain that keeps available capacity in front of customer demand. In practice, this team determines what storage costs, how it survives in the face of software and hardware failures, and how fast it is served.

Description

This is a role for an engineer who has designed, shipped, and operated the data path of a storage system at exabyte scale.

The next big challenge here is to support the industry's transition to much denser drives. This means capacity per drive is growing far faster than IOPS per drive, and maintenance operations — sealing, compaction, scrubbing, repair, rebalancing, cross-region replication — consumes that increasingly scarce IOPS budget. This is made harder by the growing demand for high-performance storage tiers by Data and AI workloads

You will own the technical agenda for solving that, across four areas:

* Storage Efficiency. Drive cost per usable byte down further: reduce replication factor without conceding the durability bar, reclaim storage overheads for compaction and other processes, and make placement maximize both space and IOPS utilization. Land support for denser and heterogeneous drive generations (CMR, HAMR, SMR) without letting IOPS-per-TB become the binding constraint on the fleet.
* Storage Integrity. Guarantee 11-nines of durability in production in the face of software and hardware failures. Own detection and repair end to end: balance detection latency against the IOPS cost of scrubbers and ensure correctness of the encode/decode/repair/rebalance paths.
* Storage Performance. Deliver differentiated performance tiers. That means improving tail latency and IOPS for the standard performance tier, while also introducing high-performance SSD-backed tiers for data and AI workloads.
* Capacity Planning and Management. Make supply closely track customer demand. Own demand forecasting, drive-generation transitions, capacity on-boarding and decommissioning, quota and rate-limit commitments, and the release value when the system is oversubscribed.

Your influence will extend well beyond ACOS. You will be the person Apple's storage organization, its hardware engineering partners, and its executives rely on for judgment on encoding, durability, and fleet efficiency.

Responsibilities

Set the Technical Agenda. Own the multi-year architecture and roadmap for how ACOS encodes, places, and serves data. Identify and prioritize the problems that matter most.
Synthesize hardware trends (HAMR, SMR, disaggregation), research and industry practice (wide-stripe coding, disk-adaptive and temperature-adaptive redundancy, tiering), and workload evolution into a strategy that keeps our storage reliability and efficiency ahead of customer requirements.
Raise the Technical Bar. Mentor and grow the most senior engineers in the org. Lead design and development for our highest-consequence systems, and set high standards for the design and operations of our services.
Drive Alignment. Broker decisions across customers, partners (SRE, hardware, capacity), and stakeholders.

Minimum Qualifications

15+ years in software development, with at least 10+ years designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed storage systems.
BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science or a related field. A PhD in distributed systems or storage is a strong plus.
Proven track record of delivering storage systems at ~exabyte scale. Your past work should demonstrate depth in erasure coding, replication, data placement, repair and reconstruction, consistency models, and consensus protocols (e.g., Paxos, Raft).
Deep, hands-on expertise in the encoding layer specifically: Reed-Solomon and Local Reconstruction Codes, wide-stripe and geo-distributed coding schemes, and the ability to reason quantitatively about the resulting durability, availability, repair-bandwidth, and IOPS trade-offs.
Familiarity with the architecture of industry-leading storage systems (e.g., Google Colossus, Ceph/RADOS, Azure Blob Storage, Amazon S3, Meta f4/Tectonic, HDFS).
Experience with the modern drive landscape and its implications: QLC and dense flash, SMR, HAMR, heterogeneous fleets, declining IOPS per TB, and disaggregated storage and compute.
Experience designing storage for high-performance workloads, particularly AI/ML or large-scale analytics. Familiarity with the I/O patterns of training pipelines, data processing engines, and high-transaction databases.
Operational credibility: you have carried a pager for a storage system at scale, and your architectural judgment is shaped by having debugged data loss and availability incidents.
Exceptional ability to influence without authority, with a history of driving major technical decisions and aligning senior engineering leaders across a large organization.
Outstanding communication skills — able to distill trade-offs for an executive audience and to hold a deep technical debate with principal-level engineers.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building out a credible, funded, multi-year path to a materially lower cost per usable byte.
In-depth understanding of maintenance overhead per usable byte trending down as drive density goes up — support denser drives.
Experience with durability guarantees measured and guaranteed in production.
Knowledge of performance tiers in production that support AI/ML and data teams.
Understanding of capacity that tracks demand within a tight band.

About the role

Anthropic’s mission is to ensure that the world safely makes the transition through transformative AI. Security is one of the clearest places where that mission plays out: the same capabilities that help attackers move faster can help defenders move faster too, and helping them use those capabilities safely and well is what this team is for. Security teams are among the earliest and most demanding users of frontier AI. They use Claude to review code at scale, find vulnerabilities before attackers do, and work through alert queues their analysts can’t keep up with. Anthropic’s Applied AI organization is building a dedicated Security team to help them do this well, and we are looking for its first leader.

You will build this team from zero. You’ll decide which security customers the team serves first, who you hire and in what order, and how the team works with Sales, Applied AI Engineering, and our security, legal, and trust partners. You’ll also stay hands-on with a few of our most important security customers, because what you learn in those accounts becomes the playbook for everyone else. You’ll also set the standard for how security customers use Claude responsibly, including where a person has to review the output before anyone acts on it.

What you’ll do

  • Hire, onboard, and develop the first Applied AI Architects on the Security team. Coach senior and early-career architects differently, and give each one clear goals.

  • Decide where the team spends its time: which segments and account types come first, which deals get architect coverage, and how to say no clearly when demand outruns headcount.

  • Partner with security account executives on joint account plans, regular pipeline and forecast reviews, and deals where the customer’s security review sets the close date.

  • Guide customers from discovery through evaluations and proofs of concept with written success criteria. Then take them from one-time code scans to sustained workloads: application security in the development lifecycle, continuous automated penetration testing, alert triage and investigation, and vulnerability and threat intelligence.

  • Work alongside the security ISVs, systems integrators, and managed security providers already in our customers’ accounts. Keep a clear line between what Anthropic delivers and what partners deliver.

  • Bring in Applied AI Engineers and our security, legal, and trust teams when a customer’s build or review needs them.

  • Write the first security playbooks, reference implementations, and evaluation approaches. Bring what you learn back to Product, Engineering, and Research, so Claude becomes more useful and more trustworthy for defenders at the same time.

  • Carry a small number of strategic security accounts yourself, from executive briefings with CISOs to hands-on workshops with their engineers.

You may be a good fit if you

  • Have 12+ years of industry experience with at least 4 years  managing a team of customer-facing technical people, such as solutions architects, sales engineers, or security consultants, and can show how the team grew and performed under you.

  • Have hands-on security depth in at least one area, such as application security, detection and response, offensive security, or vulnerability management, deep enough that practitioners trust your judgment. Application security experience highly preferred. 

  • Have used LLMs for real security work, such as code review, vulnerability discovery, triage, or investigation, and can say where they helped and where they failed.

  • Have worked large enterprise security deals end to end, including customer security reviews, in close partnership with sales.

  • Care about making AI both safe and useful for defenders, and can explain security risk and value to a CISO and to the engineers who will run the work, in terms each one cares about.

Anthropic is seeking a Regulatory Counsel to lead our legal work on AI regulation in the United States and to support our global AI regulatory posture.

In this role, you will be an in-house regulatory lawyer for Anthropic's US AI regulation and a key contributor to our global frontier AI compliance strategy. You will provide regulatory-readiness counseling as new laws are developed, day-to-day advice once they are in force, and legal support for Anthropic's non-contentious engagement with US regulators and standards bodies.   • Serve as one of Anthropic's lead in-house regulatory counsel for US AI regulation, covering applicability analysis, readiness, day-to-day advice, and compliance-program design

  • Track legislative, regulatory, and standards developments across US federal and state jurisdictions (and internationally where relevant), assess applicability and impact on Anthropic's business and products, and design compliance approaches well in advance of obligations taking effect

  • Contribute to Anthropic's global frontier AI regulatory work where it intersects with US obligations

  • Hands-on experience advising a technology business (in-house or at a leading law firm) on emerging regulatory regimes, including taking questions from first read of a statute through to a documented compliance position and a shipped artifact
  • Experience engaging with regulators, enforcement agencies, or standards bodies in a non-contentious supervisory capacity
  • Experience drafting regulatory compliance deliverables, such as compliance policies, regulatory submissions, or published compliance frameworks
  • Ability to communicate complex legal concepts clearly to technical, policy, product, and business audiences

  • 8–12 years of regulatory legal experience, with substantive depth in technology regulation and hands-on exposure to AI-specific frameworks
  • Direct experience with frontier AI regulatory regimes — California SB 53, the Colorado AI Act, or comparable state laws; or the EU AI Act and GPAI Code of Practice
  • Experience at a frontier AI company, large technology platform, or other hyper-scaling technology business operating under novel regulatory regimes
  • Familiarity with adjacent laws that intersect with AI regulation — e.g., privacy and data protection, consumer protection, product safety, and export controls
  • Familiarity with model evaluation, capability testing, or AI safety concepts
  • A background that combines private practice and in-house experience
  • Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to develop novel compliance approaches in areas without established precedent
  • Strong organizational skills to run several workstreams in parallel and keep compliance artifacts current without prompting
  • Excellence at cross-functional collaboration
  • Passion for responsible AI development and getting the balance right between innovation and appropriate safeguards
  • Understanding of how to build constructive long-term relationships with regulators and standards bodies

ABOUT THE ROLE

Anduril is seeking a Classified Cloud & Platform Engineer to design, modernize, secure, and sustain systems and infrastructure supporting classified computing environments. This systems engineering focused role spans government cloud environments, including DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5) and higher where appropriately authorized, classified cloud platforms, and on-premises classified systems. The engineer will develop secure hybrid connectivity, strengthen infrastructure automation, and support mission-critical operations in air-gapped, disconnected, and restricted-connectivity environments.


As a foundational member of the Cloud Networks team, you will assess inherited infrastructure, remediate architectural and operational deficiencies, and establish repeatable engineering and sustainment practices. You will partner with ISSMs, ISSOs, Cybersecurity, Network Engineering, and Software Engineering to modernize systems while preserving mission availability and meeting applicable authorization requirements.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Assess, design, modernize, and sustain classified cloud, hybrid, and on-premises infrastructure; identify architectural deficiencies, technical debt, security gaps, and opportunities to improve reliability, scalability, and operational efficiency.
  • Engineer government cloud infrastructure, including DoD IL5+ environments and appropriately authorized classified cloud platforms; implement secure connectivity, network segmentation, and integration with on-premises systems while respecting classification boundaries.
  • Develop Infrastructure as Code (IaC), automation, and configuration management using Terraform, Ansible, PowerShell, Python, or comparable tools; maintain version-controlled infrastructure artifacts, standardized deployments, and repeatable operational workflows suitable for restricted environments.
  • Design, deploy, and sustain Windows and Linux systems, virtualization, virtual desktop infrastructure, remote access services, and supporting platform components; integrate automation and internal tooling for provisioning, access management, and support.
  • Establish hardened system images, configuration baselines, patching and vulnerability remediation processes, and compliance validation for endpoints, servers, and applicable containerized workloads, including controlled software delivery in air-gapped environments.
  • Work directly with ISSMs, ISSOs, and Cybersecurity teams through JSIG or comparable authorization processes, including applicable RMF/DAAPM requirements; implement technical controls, document changes, support assessments, and maintain security evidence and approved baselines.
  • Establish engineering and operational standards for change control, configuration management, monitoring, logging, backup and recovery, architectural documentation, and incident response to improve supportability and mission resilience.
  • Partner with Network Engineering, Software Engineering, Cybersecurity, and Program Management to deliver secure platform integrations, plan infrastructure migrations, remediate inherited deficiencies, and shape the modernization roadmap while minimizing mission disruption.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret clearance with access to Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI), including any required program-specific access approvals.
  • Must possess or obtain and maintain a DoD 8140 compliant cybersecurity workforce qualification appropriate to the assigned role, including DOD 8570 IAT Level II equivalent certification requirements where applicable (e.g., CompTIA Security+ CE or an approved equivalent.)
  • Hands-on experience engineering or sustaining classified, air-gapped, disconnected, or similarly restricted government information systems.
  • Experience working within JSIG or comparable classified system authorization processes, coordinating technical implementation and evidence with ISSMs/ISSOs; familiarity with applicable RMF and DAAPM requirements.
  • Strong systems engineering and administration skills across Windows and Linux, enterprise virtualization, storage, and core infrastructure services.
  • Hands-on experience engineering government cloud or hybrid infrastructure, including DoD IL5+ environments or appropriately authorized classified cloud services, and secure connectivity to on-premises systems.
  • Experience modernizing existing infrastructure, diagnosing systemic technical issues, and delivering remediation with appropriate change control.
  • Experience with system hardening, DISA STIG implementation, vulnerability remediation, patch management, configuration baselines, and security control validation.
  • Hands-on experience with infrastructure automation and configuration management, including Terraform and Ansible, version-controlled IaC artifacts, and scripting with PowerShell, Python, or comparable tools.
  • Solid networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, DNS, routing, firewalls, segmentation, and secure access.
  • Understanding of identity and access management, authentication, authorization, and least-privilege principles.
  • Ability to troubleshoot cross-domain infrastructure issues, document technical decisions, and collaborate with cybersecurity and engineering stakeholders.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience supporting Special Access Program (SAP) and collateral classified environments, including working with ISSMs/ISSOs and government security stakeholders.
  • Experience with AWS GovCloud, DoD IL5+ environments, appropriately authorized classified cloud services, or other government/private cloud platforms.
  • Experience with virtual desktop infrastructure, remote application delivery, brokers, gateways, or related access services.
  • Experience with endpoint/image management and automated compliance enforcement in environments without traditional Active Directory or Group Policy.
  • Experience with Kubernetes, containers, CI/CD, artifact management, and controlled deployment processes in restricted environments.
  • Experience with infrastructure observability, centralized logging, resiliency, disaster recovery, and capacity planning.
  • Experience creating scripts, APIs, or internal platform tools; familiarity with Go, Python, or comparable languages.
  • Experience establishing technical standards and operating practices for a new or evolving engineering team.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Anduril is seeking a Classified Systems Engineer with a focus on High Performance Computing (HPC). You will work alongside senior engineers and Cybersecurity teams to build and maintain next-generation computational, networking, and storage capabilities across the enterprise.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Build and maintain scalable, hybrid HPC architectures that span on-premise and cloud environments, working within established architectural patterns
  • Support day-to-day operations of existing HPC cluster systems to ensure systems are performant and available
  • Implement and test secure multi-tenant capabilities to support consolidation of resources
  • Evaluate and test new HPC technologies, both hardware and software, and present findings to senior engineers
  • Develop expertise in HPC systems and contribute technical recommendations to the team's classified HPC strategy
  • Support DevSecOps processes and help maintain Continuous Integration / Continuous Development (CI/CD) pipelines for automating Infrastructure and Policy as Code (IaC/PaC)
  • Work with business lines and classified IT to gather requirements and help develop solutions that meet their needs on time and on budget
  • Contribute to HPC requirements documentation and support vendor evaluation efforts, including reviewing proposals and drafting Statements of Work (SOW)
  • Create and maintain training materials and runbooks to help users leverage HPC capabilities and tools for Modeling & Simulation (M&S) activities

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Knowledge of and experience with Linux Operating Systems (OS) such as Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), Rocky Linux, Ubuntu, etc.
  • Experience with automation & scripting tools such as Ansible, Terraform, Puppet, Chef, etc.
  • Familiarity with HPC technologies such as parallel/distributed file systems (e.g., Lustre, GPFS, Pure, VAST)
  • Familiarity with HPC batch scheduling software (e.g., PBSPro, SLURM)
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a US Top Secret Clearance with customer's approval

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Exposure to container orchestration, such as Kubernetes (k8s), and associated container technologies (Podman, Docker, Shifter, AppTainer/Singularity, etc.)
  • Exposure to HPC network technologies such as RDMA over Converged Ethernet Version 2 (RoCEv2), InfiniBand, Slingshot, etc.
  • Experience with bare-metal systems provisioning using tools such as xCAT, Warewulf, Bright Cluster Manager, etc.
  • Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.
  • Familiarity with software development and debugging, especially in a parallel environment
  • Familiarity with MPI and OpenMP applications and the associated configuration of libraries and dependencies
  • Awareness of NIST SP 800-53 controls and their technical implementation to meet cybersecurity requirements

ABOUT THE JOB 

Anduril is seeking a Configuration Manager.  The Configuration Manager is responsible for configuration management and change control activities.  As a Configuration Manager, you will work closely with the leaders of critical Anduril programs to manage a highly dynamic and fast-paced design, engineering, and manufacturing environment. The Configuration Manager will be the focal point for capturing and defining the baseline for a program’s requirements, design, testing, manufacturing, and sustainment data structures (requirements baseline, EBOM, MBOM, SOM, BOP). 

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

 

  • Be an integral partner to Anduril’s Product and Program Teams by:  
  • Executing configuration management activities based on the configuration management plan defined for the program. 
  • Ensuring that supported programs have robust and comprehensive configuration identification processes and documentation. 
  • Managing the end-to-end configuration control process including engineering release, facilitating critical configuration control forums such as CCB and CRB. 
  • Working with Configuration Management Analysts to build and maintain configuration status accounting dashboards ensure that critical data is captured, recorded and distributed (decisions recorded, ECRs and ECNs populated, implementation checklists written etc.) 
  • Coordinating and leading configuration audits (functional configuration audits, physical configuration audits etc.) 
  • Own end-to-end change management for key programs:  
  • Ensuring that all engineering change requests are appropriately documented, reviewed, approved, and communicated in a timely manner. 
  • Setting agendas for configuration management meetings (Technical Review Board, Change Control Board etc.) ahead of time. 
  • Generating, populating, and submitting change requests including manage compilation and synthesis of impact analyses. 
  • Be responsible for product configuration by:  
  • Analyzing product baselines (EBOM, MBOMs etc.) in Teamcenter for compliance to industry and organization standards. 
  • Supporting configuration management reviews and audits, including FCA/PCA and provide direction before, during and after the events to prevent or resolve issues. 
  • Performing periodic audits of as-built records as product definition data in Teamcenter (EBOM, MBOM etc.) 
  • Be the expert resource for the Product for Engineering Release and Change Management standards by:  
  • Modeling the use of Teamcenter software to manage Engineering changes, including part revisions, EBOM/MBOM/SBOM updates, documentation modifications, and associated workflows. 
  • Providing guidance and support to Engineering teams in configuring the Engineering, Manufacturing and Service Bills of Materials (EBOM, MBOM, SBOM). 

 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 

  • 5+ years of proven direct product configuration management experience (Product structure, parts, drawings and requirements management). 
  • 5+ years of demonstrated experience working in high complexity and high-rate production environments (aerospace, automotive, security systems, medical devices, nuclear). 
  • Familiar with configuration management principles and practices (EIA649/C, MIL-HDBK-61B). 
  • Experience with product lifecycle management (PLM) and/or data management toolsets for configuration management of complex products 
  • Possess high attention to detail and strong organizational skills. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills – you must have an ability to synthesize complex quantitative data into clear decision statements. 
  • BA/BS in an engineering discipline (Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace, Nuclear, Manufacturing) 
  • Ability to earn trust, maintain positive and professional relationships, and contribute to our inclusive culture. 
  • Is able to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Proven experience in aerospace industry 
  • Proficient in technical writing of processes and procedures 
  • Experience with Teamcenter, Teamcenter Requirements, Teamcenter Quality, Confluence & JIRA. 
  • Database skills with SQL queries, etc. 
  • Certification in CM2 or equivalent configuration management certification.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking talented Contracts Managers to support a variety of DoD, International, and Commercial contracts and programs. We are actively hiring for multiple roles across several key business lines, each offering unique technology focus areas, all on-site positions.

In this role, you will oversee the full contract lifecycle for Anduril's government and commercial contracts, ensuring compliance, minimizing risk, and optimizing contract performance. The ideal candidate will combine deep knowledge of commercial and defense contracting with strong negotiation skills and a passion for supporting national security through technological innovation.

The position will be responsible for providing contract support for various CPFF, FFP, T&M, IDIQ Government (FAR/DFARS) contracts, Other Transaction Agreements, and commercial contracts. Support of these contracts will involve proposal support, contract negotiation, contract compliance, contract management, contract modifications, and contract close-out. This role works closely with the legal and proposal teams as well as across the spectrum of Anduril’s accounting, business operations, program, and engineering teams.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Execute contract management throughout the life of each contract.
  • Complete contract review and acceptance.
  • Oversee and prepare contract proposal planning and management and support preparation of proposals.
  • Ensure compliance with government regulations, legal requirements, and company policies.
  • Assist in identification, development, and implementation of new contract policies and processes.
  • Maintain comprehensive contract documentation and compliance records.
  • Provide contract summaries and ensure contract execution in accordance with government and company requirements.
  • Provide program managers and executives with contract briefs during the life of contracts.
  • Provide guidance on FAR/DFARS requirements and other regulatory considerations.
  • Cultivate strong, ongoing relationships with internal/external customers.
  • Provide contractual guidance and risk mitigation strategies for contractual and business obligations.
  • Negotiate complex contractual terms with federal agencies, prime contractors, and subcontractors.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s Degree in business administration, government, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience with full life cycle contract management for CPFF, FFP, and T&M government and commercial contracts.
  • A strong working knowledge of US Government contracting including FAR/DFARS experience.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Exceptional analytical and problem-solving abilities. You are highly respected amongst your peers and/or counterparts and known as someone who gets things done.
  • U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export-controlled data.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.
  • Location: Based in Costa Mesa, CA, Washington, DC, or Ashville, OH.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with U.S. DoD major weapons platforms.
  • NCMA Certifications including but not limited to CPCM, CFCM, or CCCM.
  • Graduate degree in business, law, government, or a related field.
  • Experience with Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), FAR cost allowability rules, and Certified Cost or Pricing Data Proposals.
  • Secret or Top Secret Clearance.

Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril is the world’s fastest-growing defense technology company, bringing Silicon Valley talent and funding to the defense and security sectors. Our technology helps the United States and its allies solve their hardest national security challenges by enabling operators to make better, more informed decisions in life-and-death situations. We have assembled a diverse team of experts in artificial intelligence, computer vision, sensor fusion, optics, and data analysis that are creating software and hardware solutions to radically evolve the capabilities of the United States, our allies, and commercial customers. If you are passionate about solving problems that have a real impact, come join Anduril and build the future of defense.

A critical part of the Anduril team is its Contracts Managers, who play a crucial role in program success. They interface daily with a motivated team of program leadership, functional leadership, and customers in fast-paced environments.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking talented Contracts Managers to support a variety of DoD, International, and Commercial contracts and programs. For our Reston, VA location we are actively hiring for our Intelligence Systems business line, focusing on rapid development programs. This role requires active clearance and experience with Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs). You will oversee the full contract lifecycle for Anduril's government and commercial contracts, ensuring compliance, minimizing risk, and optimizing contract performance. The ideal candidate will combine deep knowledge of commercial and defense contracting with strong negotiation skills and a passion for supporting national security through technological innovation.

This position will be responsible for providing contract support for various CPFF, FFP, T&M, IDIQ Government (FAR/DFARS) contracts, Other Transaction Agreements, and commercial contracts. Support of these contracts will involve proposal support, contract negotiation, contract compliance, contract management, contract modifications, and contract close-out. This role works closely with the legal and proposal teams as well as across the spectrum of Anduril’s accounting, business operations, program, and engineering teams.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Execute contract management throughout the life of each contract.
  • Complete contract review and acceptance.
  • Oversee and prepare contract proposal planning and management and support preparation of proposals.
  • Ensure compliance with government regulations, legal requirements, and company policies.
  • Assist in identification, development, and implementation of new contract policies and processes.
  • Maintain comprehensive contract documentation and compliance records.
  • Provide contract summaries and ensure contract execution in accordance with government and company requirements.
  • Provide program managers and executives with contract briefs during the life of contracts.
  • Provide guidance on FAR/DFARS requirements and other regulatory considerations.
  • Cultivate strong, ongoing relationships with internal/external customers.
  • Provide contractual guidance and risk mitigation strategies for contractual and business obligations.
  • Negotiate complex contractual terms with federal agencies, prime contractors, and subcontractors.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s Degree in business administration, government, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience with full life cycle contract management for CPFF, FFP, and T&M government and commercial contracts.
  • A strong working knowledge of US Government contracting including FAR/DFARS experience.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Exceptional analytical and problem-solving abilities. You are highly respected amongst your peers and/or counterparts and known as someone who gets things done.
  • U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export-controlled data.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.
  • Location: Based in Reston, VA with travel to DC

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with U.S. DoD major weapons platforms.
  • NCMA Certifications including but not limited to CPCM, CFCM, or CCCM.
  • Graduate degree in business, law, government, or a related field.
  • Experience with Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), FAR cost allowability rules, and Certified Cost or Pricing Data Proposals.
  • Secret or Top Secret Clearance.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Director of Finance to lead financial planning, reporting, and cost strategy for RMS, HW Eng, and SWP. You will own the P&L and investment planning for these platform organizations, and you will be the leader Divisions turn to when they want to understand the ROI of these shared capabilities. This role requires equal comfort operating as an internal finance business partner to platform leadership and as an honest broker to the Divisions that platform teams serve.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own financial planning, forecasting, and monthly/quarterly reporting, including budget development and variance analysis against plan
  • Design and maintain the cost allocation and chargeback methodology used to bill platform costs back to Divisions and BLs, ensuring the methodology is transparent, defensible, and auditable
  • Build unit-economics and make-vs-buy analyses that quantify whether centralized capacity delivers a real cost or speed advantage over a Division/BL building or sourcing the capability independently
  • Develop the capacity planning and prioritization framework platform leadership uses to sequence competing demand across Divisions and BLs, and translate resulting trade-offs into financial terms for company leadership
  • Partner directly with Division finance leads and business leaders as internal customers, proactively communicating cost trends and variances before they surface as surprises in business reviews
  • Build performance dashboards and KPIs (unit cost (APUC), utilization, throughput, cost trend vs. alternatives) that make platform performance transparent to non-platform stakeholders
  • Develop ROI and payback analyses to support capacity investment decisions, including new equipment, facilities, and headcount
  • Partner with platform engineering and operations leadership on strategic decisions, including build-vs-buy, insourcing/outsourcing, and capacity expansion

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10+ years of progressive finance experience, including exposure to manufacturing, hardware engineering, or government contracting environments
  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field
  • Experience building or operating cost allocation, shared-services, or chargeback models within a multi-business-unit organization
  • Strong financial modeling skills, including the ability to independently build unit-economics and make-vs-buy analyses
  • Demonstrated ability to partner with both technical/engineering leadership and finance peers across other business units
  • Advanced Excel and financial systems/ERP proficiency
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Prior experience in a shared-services, platform, or internal-supplier finance role, including experience being evaluated by internal customers with real alternatives to the service provided
  • Familiarity with aerospace/defense manufacturing cost structures
  • MBA, CPA, or CFA
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
